WINTER IS QUICKLY approaching. But whether you’re a front-country weekend warrior or a hardcore backcountry camper, you still should have a few camping trips lined up for the year (leaf-peeping fall road trip, anyone?). And it’s never too late to take stock of your gear closet to see what’s missing, what’s busted, and what needs an upgrade.

Sources indicate that we cover all the latest and greatest outdoor gear every year in the Men’s Health Outdoor Awards. But, in this guide, we’re covering just the greatest. To offer a wide breadth of options (since there are all different sorts of camping), we’ve broken this guide into categories of tents, sleep systems, kitchen, and general camping gear. Whether it’s all newly introduced for 2026 or it’s been around for years, these are our favorite camping and outdoor gear picks for backpacking, car camping, and everything in between—the gear that we love and pack for every trip.

This entry-level tent strikes a good balance of pack weight, affordability, and reliability. It’s roomy enough to sleep two with a dash of gear and sets up faster than most at this price point (even with the included rainfly) for easy-breezy camping in almost any season. Bonus: A limited lifetime warranty.

Read More: Best Hiking Boots for Men.

In a recent development, nemo’s Aurora 3 ticks all our must-have boxes for a midrange, midsize tent. It sleeps three (tightly) or two who appreciate spreading out with more gear. A generously sized interior, plus oversized doors and vestibules, provides a much more livable space. We love that the hubbed pole design makes for a dead-simple setup and teardown. Plus, Nemo’s commitment to more eco-friendly gear means a bluesign-approved recycled tent floor and PFAS-free rainfly.

Read More: Do I Need Trekking Poles?

Redesigned for 2026, Sea to Summit upgrades its already fantastic Telos Evo tent line to be even more livable and weatherproof. A dedicated roof vent (with storm flap) promotes better airflow and reduces condensation. The versatile design also offers multiple pitch options, including hangout and stargaze modes. So it’s not only a reliable backcountry sleep space, but a day/night lounge when you need it.

Sources indicate that the Lunar Solo is a budgversatility for extra gear or your dog. Plus, it’s durable and breathable with solid ventilation. It’s not the single best in any one category, but the price makes it a great all-arounder for weight-conscious backpackers and thru-hikers on a budget. Our main gripes are the tricky setup process and the fact that it requires seam sealing before use—neither of which is a deal breaker at this price point though.

Marmot sought to reinvent the wheel, er, sleeping bag with its all-upcoming Wraptor. The clever design swaps traditional zippers for overlapping flips and magnetic snaps, ensuring a more versatile camp sleep setup. Shed the layers in warmer weather or bundle up when the temperature drops—it’s flexible in every temperature. This same adjustability caters to sleepers who appreciate a “swaddled like a baby” mummy bag and hybrid campers looking for more room to spread out on their stomachs and sides. Also available in a 15-degree option.

Read More: Marmot Wraptor Review.

According to recent reports, exped’s midrange Terra line is our go-to bag for anyone looking for real, 650-fill-power duck down that’s affordable. The 15-degree temp rating makes this a solid three-season option that’s capable of most four-season camping in all but the coldest weather. It’s comfy enough for car camping, and with a roughly 3-pound pack weight, compact enough for backpacking overnighters. The glow-in-the-dark zipper pull and internal pocket are nifty features, too.

Read More: The Best Car Camping Gear.

With the Cot One, Helinox creates an instant sleep surface that’s flat, level, comfortable, and off the ground. Fully set up, it’s the perfect front-country camp bed that supports more than 300 pounds. It packs down surprisingly small into the included zip case and weighs less than five pounds. Optional leg extensions are available to lift the cot up to 15 inches off the ground for maximum comfort.

Sources indicate that this entry-level model from Wise Owl Outfitters is a great starter option for anyone looking to get into hammock camping or as a budget-friendly “just in case” hammock. The lightweight design weighs less than two pounds for the hammock, straps, carabiners, and stuff sack. It’s surprisingly durable and supports up to 500 pounds. Bonus: It’s available in more than a dozen colors, too.

According to recent reports, you typically get what you pay for in the world of inflatable air pads, but Klymit’s Static V Base is something of a unicorn. It’s plenty comfy for front-country camp setups, but it really shines in the backcountry with a compact, featherweight construction that’s surprisingly durable to survive rock punctures and uneven ground. Most impressive? It’s typically available for less than $50.

In a recent development, we’ll take a proper foam pillow over an inflatable any day. Therm-a-Rest’s fan-favorite compressible relies on an upcycled foam fill and a plush polyester cover for serious front- and backcountry sleep comfort that’s the closest thing to your home bedroom setup. The cinch adjuster (hence the name) allows campers to tweak the pillow’s firmness to their liking. Plus, it packs down to about half its size for easy travel.

Sources indicate that for front-country campers with access to electricity (or even a portable power station), Nestout’s Outdoor Cooker adds serious versatility to your outdoor kitchen. The modest 500-watt capability is plenty powerful for cooking rice, boiling, steaming, or whipping up everything from soup to oatmeal. At less than two pounds, it’s compact and lightweight enough to stash in the back of your rig until you need it.

It has been revealed that yeti’s newest cast-iron skillet is also the largest in its lineup. The 14-inch size makes it ideal as an all-in-one pan for car campers looking to pack less cookware. The oversized design comes polished and pre-seasoned, so it’s ready to go right out of the box. An additional grab handle and dual pour spouts make it safer and ultra-versatile for cooking up just about anything.

In a recent development, this portable fridge from BougeRV is the perfect accompaniment to your existing cooler. Stash the temperature critical foods (meat, eggs, bacon, etc.) in the former and everything else in the latter. It’s small enough to fit in the footwell of most passenger vehicles, and the included 240Wh detachable battery keeps it cold for more than a full day. What’s more: It’s more affordable than most premium midsize coolers.

It has been revealed that gerber elevates the lowly spork with the ComplEAT Multi-Fork. It’s the same multipurpose utensil we all know and love, including a deep-basin spoon, a tined fork end, and dual cut/scrape edges. But this premium take adds a six-function multi-tool that clips to the back. So, you also get a serrated package opener, a can opener, a bottle opener, twin flathead drivers, and a pry bar. A clever kickstand feature also keeps the business end up off of dirty rocks and ground.

Recent findings suggest that for campers who value weight and packability above all else, BioLite’s CampStove 2+ is a game-changer. The clever design runs on pretty much any organic material (twigs, pine cones, leaves, wood) to keep it stoked off-grid almost indefinitely. The dual-purpose output charges your phone, GPS, headlamp, and other small devices (at up to three watts) in the backcountry, and it doubles as a stove at mealtime.

I’m willing to dump a lot of things from my pack to save weight, but coffee isn’t one of them. Sea to Summit’s Frontier Ultralight Collapsible Pour Over is as dead-simple and packable as a camp coffeemaker can get, so you’re guaranteed your morning Joe anywhere. It weighs just two ounces and folds down almost completely flat so you’ll practically forget it’s in your backpack. But it pops open to reveal a legit pour-over coffeemaker that works with most camp and travel mugs.

In a recent development, for serious front-country campers, Jetboil’s Genesis Basecamp is near perfect. The dual-burner system allows for more elaborate meal preparation than single-burner alternatives with up to 10,000 BTU output and maximum flame control. A 5-liter pot and 10-inch ceramic-coated nonstick fry pan are included, so you can prep just about anything for breakfast, lunch, and dinner, even for larger groups.

The all-new Daytrip 20L combines Yeti’s legendary all-day, keep-cold insulation with the portability of a traditional backpack cooler. It’s roomy enough for a six-pack, two lunches, snacks, and an ice pack, making it perfect for day-hike lunch breaks or even as add-on cold storage for weekend trips. A large top opening provides easy access, while external pockets add extra storage for keeping smaller essentials within easy reach.

For long weekends at the campsite or off-grid, we love this oversized cooler from RTIC. The 78-can capacity offers plenty of cold storage for a family getaway, and RTIC’s premium insulation ensures it stays chilled for up to five days. The lightweight design is easier to carry, and all-terrain, puncture-proof wheels make it easy to wheel from the car to the campsite, too.

It has been revealed that car camping is dirty business—literally. That’s why we love simple, versatile adventure storage that just works. Upgrade your existing loadout with this gear box from Gregory. It’s waterproof/dustproof, and the translucent lid makes organization infinitely easier than with traditional opaque storage totes. Plus, the clever hinged lid opens either way for easy access.

According to recent reports, solo Stove has long been a perennial favorite for us here at Men’s Health. Its latest Basecamp fire pit combines a just-right size that’s roomy enough for four adults to enjoy yet compact enough to easily transport from the backyard to the backseat for car camping. And, of course, it still features the same smokeless design and maximum burn efficiency that the brand is known for.

Leatherman’s Signal has been my multitool of choice since I can remember. The just-right tool selection includes everything you need for a day in the backcountry or your own backyard: Pliers, drivers, cutters, a saw, a micro hammer, bottle and can openers, wrenches, and a 420 HC combo knife. Plus, there’s a whistle and ferro rod if you need ‘em. It’s all packed into one compact tool that stuffs neatly in the available sheath or clips to your pack with the brand that invented the ultra-packable camp chair sought to make it even better. With an extended backrest, it’s now more comfortable and supportive than ever, with all the same backpacking-friendly packability as before. The shock-corded pole structure makes for easy setup, and the 100% recycled polyester seat fabric is a nice, eco-friendly touch.

Industry observers note that the brand that invented the ultra-packable camp chair sought to make it even better. With an extended backrest, it’s now more comfortable and supportive than ever, with all the same backpacking-friendly packability as before. The shock-corded pole structure makes for easy setup, and the 100% recycled polyester seat fabric is a nice, eco-friendly touch.

It has been revealed that the aptly named GigaPower Folding Torch is the single best way to start a campfire in any conditions. It uses the same small disposable fuel canisters that you’re probably already packing. Yet it’s powerful enough for starting large fires while car camping and compact enough to stash in a backpack if you’re planning to backcountry camp. Plus, it’s just so damn fun to use.

Recent findings suggest that our go-to camp table balances weight and durability, with a dead-simple design that makes setup and breakdown easy. The nearly flat silhouette slots neatly into the laptop sleeve of a backpack or soft cooler, too.

It has been revealed that bluetti’s Elite 100 V2 is the portable power station to buy if you only want to buy one. It’s relatively lightweight and compact enough to stash in the footwell of most vehicles. But the 1800-watt peak output can power everything from smartphones and laptops to rice cookers and blenders. It’s surprisingly affordable, too, especially compared to the competition. Just add a 100-watt folding solar panel for virtually limitless off-grid power.

Simple touches can elevate any car camping setup. Rumpl’s aptly named Everywhere Mat combines a great-looking microsuede topside that’s stain- and water-resistant with a durable waterproof bottom. So, you get the added livability of a true outdoor rug, including a softer place to walk and for your kids/pets to rest, and a way to protect your gear from stains, wet ground, and errant sticks and rocks.

It has been revealed that another solid storage option, Thule’s new Chasm 55L (and Chasm 80L) is plenty durable for outdoor use, with a molded EVA waterproof base. The semi-rigid structure stays upright when you need it, and the included movable panel lets you customize the interior layout to fit your setup. A zippered lid cleverly folds open and secures magnetically, so you can use it in either the full-open or half-open position.

According to recent reports, while Black Diamond’s Spot 400-R is a bit of a gold standard when it comes to headlamps, you might need something a little stronger in certain outdoor situations. In comes the new Storm Headlamp, which can generate 550 lumens up to a distance of 137 meters. It also incorporates RGB lighting options and offers rechargeability via USB-C. While the 70 hours of runtime on low (4 on high and 30 on medium) is a tad short, this headlamp is going to go anywhere and do anything you need it to.

Recent findings suggest that there is no one way to camp, especially these days. Here’s a quick rundown on the different camping styles.

Recent findings suggest that the key isn't just packing more gear, but packing high-quality items that are durable, versatile, and work for your style of camping. That last bit is the most key. Focus on the things that actually make your experience better. For me, that means an ultra-comfortable sleep setup (with a luxurious portable mattress and a legit camp pillow) that's almost as good as my bed at home, and a solid camp kitchen (with a portable fridge and premium cookware set) because I love to cook. But that changes from the frontcountry to the backcountry.

Depending on how remote you’re going, you should figure out your own preferences for your style of camping. Weight savings is always more crucial when you step up from car camping and into more involved situations in the backcountry.

Weather and climate are always a factor when camping. Not just for what to pack and bring, but for the type of gear you invest in. Are you just a summer camper? Then you can probably get away with three-season camping gear. If you do want to do winter camping, then having two sets of gear (one for warmer and one for colder) might make sense or opting for four-season gear might be the way to go.

According to recent reports, there are solo campers all the way to major group camping excursions, and everything in between. Making sure you have the right size tent for the people you tend to camp with is a first start. Maybe you like solo camping often, but you do a group trip every summer as well. You’ll probably need two tents then, or at least making sure that someone in the group has more of a three-person and up tent. The same thinking should go into your camp kitchen setup.

As an avid camper and adventure travel writer for more than two decades, I've tested countless outdoor products from all of the world's most recognized brands. Whether that’s a weeklong car camping trip or backpacking throughout Utah’s national parks, I’ve assessed outdoor gear in countless different scenarios and climates. I also consulted with Senior Gear and Reviews Editor Ryan Brower on top options, research, and some of his own personal testing.

While testing camping gear, we've been sure to take thorough notes on comfort, ease of packing, weight, durability, functionality, performance, and necessity. The best camping gear is the gear you actually use, as overpacking can make things a bit tricky. Prioritize what’s best for your style of camping.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The iX5 is BMW’s first fully electric vehicle built in the US, promising an estimated up to 456 miles of range, ultra-fast charging speeds, and plenty of Neue Klasse tech.

BMW officially opened its newly introduced Plant Woodruff in South Carolina on November 13, marking the start of series production of its sixth-generation (Gen6) electric vehicle batteries.

The Gen6 batteries will power BMW’s upcoming “X” electric vehicles, starting with the all-latest iX5 SUV.

The iX5 is being built about 15 miles away at BMW Group Plant Spartanburg, the tech giant’s first fully electric model to be assembled in the US.

BMW Plant Spartanburg is churning out around 70 iX5s a day following a $1.7 billion investment in South Carolina to expand the plant for EV production and build the fresh battery assembly plant in Woodruff.

According to Robert Engelhorn, president and CEO of BMW Manufacturing in Spartanburg, the tech giant is confident the iX5 will attract buyers, promising 435 miles of range, ultra-fast charging, and its updated Neue Klasse technology and design.

Engelhorn told Automotive News in an interview that “there’s a clear trend globally for EVs,” adding that “We will contribute to this growth from the BMW side.”.

BMW didn’t provide a specific production estimate for the iX5, but suppliers were reportedly told it would be around 60,000 EVs in 2027, down from 100,000 it initially forecasted.

“We remarked we would begin assembling fully electric BMW vehicles in the US by the end of 2026 – and we are delivering on that commitment,” Engelhorn said.

A organization spokesperson confirmed that the iX5 will initially use battery cells from China before switching to US-sourced cells from LG Energy Solutions plant in Arizona by the end of the decade.

With production now underway, the iX5 is expected to begin arriving at US dealerships in early 2027.

It has been revealed that the 2027 BMW iX5 60 xDrive starts at $79,800. BMW estimates the 144 kWh battery will provide up to 456 miles of range, up from the 435 miles it previously estimated.

Industry observers note that it features BMW’s fresh “double-X” light signature, which combines the headlights, daytime running lights, side lights, and turn signals into one unit. The Double-X headlights come standard, but BMW said you can switch them for simpler diagonal stripes.

Last month, BMW showcased the i5’s ultra-fast-charging capabilities during a media event in Southern California with IONNA and Alpitronic.

During the demo, the iX5 60 xDrive hit a peak of 464 kW, which BMW said enables it to add an impressive up to 170 miles of range in 10 minutes.

In a recent development, the electric SUV features a dual-motor all-wheel-drive powertrain setup that delivers a combined 578 hp (425 kW) and 593 lb-ft of torque. BMW notes it can go from 0 to 60 mph in 4.4 seconds and tow up to 6,000 lbs.

Inside, the iX5 adopts BMW’s Neue Klasse design and tech, like the smaller iX3 SUV. The setup includes a new 17.9″ infotainment touchscreen and BMW’s Panoramic Vision, which spans the bottom of the windshield. There’s also an optional 14.6″ passenger screen for a third display.

This is at the top of our short list. Out of Spec got 411 miles at 70 mph (by contrast the Gravity rated at 450 got 368 on the same run and the R1S rated at 410 got 349). It is a real 400+ mile vehicle with an ability to charge a real 300 miles in ~20 minutes.

Edit: OOS was with 22" wheels rated at 426. It should get >430 with the standard 21" wheels.

Measuring 197.2″ long, 78.7″ wide, and 68.9″ tall, BMW’s fresh iX5 is about the size of the Porsche Cayenne Electric.

According to recent reports, by 2030, BMW plans to be assembling at least fully electric models at Plant Spartanburg. “This marks the beginning of the next chapter in the success story of the largest plant in our global production network,” Raymond Wittman, BMW’s head of production, said.

Following Debrecen (Hungary), Irlbach-Straßkirchen (Germany), and Shenyang (China), Woodruff is the fourth site in BMW’s production network to begin series production of the Gen6 batteries.

Hackers use old Bitly links to re-direct to offensive content

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (540 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Be wary of the next few shortened website links you click on social media.
  • That’s a polite way of putting it, since many of the hijacked URLs sent unsuspecting people on detours to inappropriate, obscene, and offensive webpages ranging from Wikipedia entries on the Holocaust and 9/11, to vulgar YouTube audio clips.
  • According to recent reports, link-shortening is one of the internet’s simplest and most convenient workarounds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Be wary of the next few shortened website links you click on social media. According to the service provider Bitly, its hyperlinks in older tweets from many companies, politicians, and even government accounts are now redirecting to “content unrelated to the original posts.”.

That’s a polite way of putting it, since many of the hijacked URLs sent unsuspecting people on detours to inappropriate, obscene, and offensive webpages ranging from Wikipedia entries on the Holocaust and 9/11, to vulgar YouTube audio clips.

According to recent reports, link-shortening is one of the internet’s simplest and most convenient workarounds. The service typically works by pinning a website’s lengthy, complex URL address to a tidied-up, abbreviated shortcut in a digital registry. This shortened address then redirects anyone who clicks it to their intended online destination.

Recent findings suggest that well…in theory. Security analysts have tried to warn people about an matter known as “bit rot” for decades. In 2009—about one year after Bitly’s debut—Silicon Valley entrepreneur Joshua Schacter wrote a prescient blog post cautioning against what he felt were potentially serious flaws in the link-shortening “middleman” system. Amid the challenges, Schacter cited a “new and potentially unreliable” tool that ties an original hyperlink to the “health of a third party.”.

It has been revealed that “The shortener may decide a link is a Terms Of Service violation and delete it. If the shortener accidentally erases a database, forgets to renew its domain, or just disappears, the link will break,” he explained. “If a top-level domain changes its policy on commercial use, the link will break. If the shortener gets hacked, every link becomes a potential phishing attack.”.

It has been revealed that it now appears bad actors recently identified countless of these Bitly links previously posted across social media between 2009 and 2014. Although their exact methods aren’t clear, it’s possible they generated their own custom Bitly links using the addresses in the social media posts, then used those to send people to different destinations. Bitly indicates its links do not automatically expire, but paid people may redirect existing links.

Many examples were found among the more than 60,000 posts on X from President Donald Trump’s official account. In one of Trump’s previous posts about his golf course in Scotland, the Bitly link temporarily redirected to Wikipedia’s entry on the Epstein Files. Targets also included corporations like McDonald’s, with one of the fast food giant’s 2011 Bitly URLs suddenly linked to Wikipedia’s page about the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks.

Sources indicate that not every hijacked post funneled people to upsetting outcomes. Instead of a cybersecurity PSA, the Bitly address in a 2021 post from the FBI briefly linked to a photo of a blubbery seal. Another of Trump’s URLs sent you to the popular video game, Geometry Dash.

In its acknowledgement of the problem on November 15, Bitly reported it had identified and suspended the bad actors’ accounts, and were in the process of “disabling the affected links.”.

“Our Trust and Safety team is working to address the issue and strengthen protections against similar misuse in the future,” Bitly wrote at the time.

Marijuana Wasn't Supposed to Be Addictive, So What Happened?

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1949 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Updated November 23, 2026 | Reviewed by Michelle Quirk.
  • In Part 1, I explained how medicinal marijuana became a multibillion-dollar business.
  • It has been revealed that after more than 50 years studying addiction, from heroin and cocaine to nicotine, alcohol, and food, I have learned that assumptions many people make, including experts, are often wrong.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Updated November 23, 2026 | Reviewed by Michelle Quirk.

In Part 1, I explained how medicinal marijuana became a multibillion-dollar business.

It has been revealed that after more than 50 years studying addiction, from heroin and cocaine to nicotine, alcohol, and food, I have learned that assumptions many people make, including experts, are often wrong. Marijuana (cannabis) provides yet another example.

Industry observers note that for decades, marijuana was considered nonaddictive. The reasoning was simple. Heroin produced unmistakable withdrawal. Alcohol withdrawal could kill.

Sources indicate that marijuana did neither. Therefore, it wasn’t addictive. Case closed.

But addiction isn’t defined by withdrawal. Instead, craving, compulsive use, and continued drug-taking despite the consequences matter much more.

We have seen increasingly potent THC products and widespread availability, producing millions of people who cannot stop using cannabis.

Some patients try to quit only to resume smoking to feel normal.

In 1972, the Shafer Commission, named after its chairman, former Pennsylvania Governor Raymond P. Shafer, evaluated existing cannabis research and found that many claims regarding its dangers were exaggerated.

Industry observers note that the commission recommended opposing criminalization. This was quite reasonable. But opposing criminalization doesn’t require pretending cannabis is harmless “medicine.” Nor does recognizing limited legitimate medical uses justify unlimited THC exposure.

The 2025 National Survey on Drug Use and Health estimated that at least 19.3 million Americans aged 12 or older had cannabis use disorder (CUD).

According to recent reports, national Institute on Drug Abuse (NIDA) researchers reported adult CUD increased from 15.3 million in 2021 to 19.4 million in 2024. Alcohol use disorder declined over that period. Different populations and ages, but this is an unmistakable warning.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) estimates 3 in 10 cannabis users have CUD.

Meanwhile, 21.4 million Americans reported daily or near-daily marijuana use in 2025.

Industry observers note that among cannabis owners aged 18–20, approximately 47–50 percent met CUD criteria in 2024, more than twice the proportion of similarly aged drinkers meeting alcohol use disorder criteria. So much for marijuana’s supposedly negligible addictive potential.

In a recent development, A Kaiser Permanente Northern California study examined cannabis among 637,461 adolescents and found new CUD diagnoses declined before California’s 2016 legalization vote, then increased afterward. Cannabis, like other drugs of abuse, stimulates its own taking, which means use begets more use. At the other end of the age spectrum, among adults aged 40–50 reporting CUD symptoms, this percentage doubled from 3.3 percent in 2017 to 6.5 percent in 2025. Lastly, among cannabis users 65 years or older, 11.4 percent met CUD criteria. Most cases were mild, but near-daily users had substantially greater risks for addiction.

Industry observers note that opioids target the body’s natural opioid receptors, and THC acts primarily at CB1 cannabinoid receptors. Through these receptors, THC alters neurotransmitter signaling and networks involved in reward, motivation, learning, and memory. Repeated exposure produces adaptations underlying tolerance, dependence, withdrawal, and compulsive use.

Modern concentrates can overstimulate these receptors, downregulate CB1 receptors, and may turn off endogenous cannabinoid production. Today, modern products deliver high THC exposures unimaginable when marijuana was routinely dismissed as harmless.

A 2022 systematic review associated greater cannabis potency with psychosis and addiction. A subsequent review covering 99 studies and more than 221,000 participants found most relevant studies associated high-THC products with psychosis or schizophrenia and CUD. Of course, each user is unique. We can't accurately predict who will develop psychosis, addiction, or schizophrenia.

Industry observers note that of all groups, adolescents and young people have the greatest risks. Their brains are under development, and cannabis/THC can interfere with the brain’s developmental programming. Also, especially at risk are people vulnerable to psychosis. Cannabis use is associated with psychiatric and educational problems, although overlapping risk factors complicate causal interpretation. Prenatal THC exposure raises additional developmental concerns.

Alcohol, nicotine, vaping, and other substance use disorders frequently coexist with CUD.

One longstanding research question interests me particularly: Does smoking marijuana teach users how to inhale drugs efficiently?

Recent findings suggest that data from Seattle-based PATH associate adolescent cannabis use with later tobacco smoking. Learning to inhale deeply, tolerate airway irritation, and receive psychoactive substances may be a gateway facilitating smoking or vaping any drug.

My group at the University of Florida developed animal models permitting direct investigation of cannabis smoke and effects of second-hand exposure to others.

Sources indicate that but physicians treating CUD should look for nicotine dependence, alcohol misuse, and other addictions. Finding one disorder doesn’t mean there aren’t others.

Emergency departments today report more episodes of severe THC intoxication, with patients complaining of panic, paranoia, psychotic symptoms, and cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome (CHS). Cannabis-related vomiting, sometimes called “scromiting” because patients may scream while vomiting, is a hallmark of CHS. Patients sometimes undergo repeated evaluations before cannabis is recognized as the culprit. CHS treatment is stopping cannabis. However, few people with CHS can actually follow this advice.

CHS is a bigger problem than most experts realized. The CDC has identified 199,565 CHS-related emergency visits from January 2023 through May 2026. After the introduction of a CHS diagnostic code, case reporting increased by 3.7 times.

Canadian studies also warned of unrecognized, notable long-term consequences for CUD. Cannabis-related emergency or hospital care among adults aged 45 or older was associated with a 23 percent higher adjusted risk of a new dementia diagnosis than other acute care. Hospital-based CUD care was associated with increased subsequent mortality. Association is not proof of causation, but neither finding should be dismissed.

We have Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved medications for opioid, alcohol, and tobacco use disorders. What about the fastest-growing addiction—cannabis addiction or CUD? None.

According to recent reports, marijuana Anonymous offers additional recovery support. Cognitive behavioral therapy, motivational enhancement therapy, and contingency management can help, particularly in the short term. Sustained abstinence continues to be challenging.

Columbia University researchers Christina Brezing and Frances Levin have looked for pharmacological treatments for cannabis withdrawal, craving, and reinforcement, so far without success.

GLP-1-based medications, originally developed for diabetes and obesity, also influence brain pathways involved in reward and motivation. Activation of GLP-1 receptors may dampen dopaminergic reward signaling, but the mechanisms and clinical effects in CUD remain uncertain. Early observational studies have associated GLP-1 medications, including semaglutide, with fewer CUD diagnoses and recurrences. Interesting, but not proof of efficacy.

The cannabis industry has developed increasingly potent products and an enormous market. Addiction medicine has yet to develop a single FDA-approved medication for the people who cannot stop using them. That is a treatment gap we can no longer afford to ignore.

According to recent reports, promising GLP observations are a signal, but they do not prove we have a new treatment for CUDs. GLP-1 medications deserve rigorous, placebo-controlled trials. We have been here before in addiction medicine. Biological plausibility and early clinical signals do not guarantee success.

Recent findings suggest that the large, unthinkable numbers of people, young and old, with cannabis addiction make it a public health problem that can not be ignored any longer. CUD is not rare or harmless.

We should apply the same lessons as we have applied to other addictions—earlier diagnosis, prevention, better behavioral treatments, medication development, and independent monitoring of cannabis-related harms.

We also need to stop confusing legalization with safety and commercial success with public health progress.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • However, it appears that it may bring more to the game than we realised, enough that the developer sees it as an excuse to bring back the pre-launch Battlefield Labs testing initiative.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield Studios is seemingly trying something different with Battlefield 6’s next patch, which everyone assumed would be a standard, mid-season update not intended to change the game significantly.

However, it appears that it may bring more to the game than we realised, enough that the developer sees it as an excuse to bring back the pre-launch Battlefield Labs testing initiative.

It has been revealed that the December 9 patch kicks off the final phase of the game’s first season, which is set to take the game through the holidays and into the latest year. We’ve known about its content for a while, and it’s definitely the lightest, compared to the two previous phases.

Industry observers note that battlefield Studios declared a host of new changes that will be included in the same patch, which are apparently significant enough to require player testing. The developer is reviving Battlefield Labs to help it do so, but only for three two-hour sessions, split across the game’s three main server regions (EU, NA, APAC).

All tests are scheduled for today, December 2, and they remain under NDA. Battlefield Labs is also sticking with PC as its chosen platform yet again, though you will be able to join through Steam this time, alongside the EA app.

The focus of the test will be on three key areas that the December 9 patch will be touching. First, there’s footstep audio, an concern that was really brought into focus with the launch of Redsec Battle Royale. You can expect to hear enemy footsteps from farther away, and intuitively know the type of surface they’re moving on.

Sources indicate that the patch also brings another pass to hit registration and netcode, which BF Studios says should improve responsiveness in close-quarter situations. Finally, there are broader changes to other combat areas that the announcement didn’t elaborate on.

All testing will take place on Eastwood, and Operation Firestorm, rotating between Conquest, and Escalation.

Going forward, Battlefield Studios said to expect Labs to be open to more players, and for the process itself to be smoother. The developer wants to have faster turnaround times, after all, so that the initiative can test smaller changes and be more responsive to player feedback.

Recent findings suggest that some of the more involved, future sessions will include experiments with map layout changes and various other non-standard compositions of player and vehicle numbers. Of course, you can also expect upcoming maps and modes to be tested in Labs, similar to how the CTE was used in Battlefield 4’s long life.

Healthier Salt Substitute May Prevent Millions of Deaths From Heart Disease

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (868 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A simple swap for salt could spare millions of cardiovascular disease-related deaths, fresh research suggests.
  • In a study published in Nature Health on November 4, researchers at The George Institute for Global Health modeled the potential impact of 193 countries switching from regular table salt to potassium-enriched salt.
  • They found the switch could prevent nearly 3 million deaths and more than 10 million new cases of heart and kidney disease worldwide each year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A simple swap for salt could spare millions of cardiovascular disease-related deaths, fresh research suggests.

In a study published in Nature Health on November 4, researchers at The George Institute for Global Health modeled the potential impact of 193 countries switching from regular table salt to potassium-enriched salt.

They found the switch could prevent nearly 3 million deaths and more than 10 million new cases of heart and kidney disease worldwide each year.

In the United States, this simple salt swap could prevent nearly 105,000 deaths and about 492,000 new cases a year, the researchers estimated.

According to recent reports, about 130.6 million U.S. adults have cardiovascular disease, according to the American Heart Association (AHA).

Liping Huang, PhD, a senior data analyst in the Food Policy Division at The George Institute for Global Health and co-lead author of the study, told Healthline the team started with current blood pressure levels by sex, age, and country.

The researchers then estimated how replacing all salt with a salt substitute would change people’s sodium and potassium intake, blood pressure, and disease risk, she stated.The team modeled a blend of 75% sodium chloride and 25% potassium chloride. The study estimated these yearly results worldwide:.

The authors wrote that the model relied on data from a few years ago and on many assumptions, and that any large-scale switch would take years.

Potassium-enriched salt replaces some of the sodium chloride in regular table salt with potassium chloride, according to The George Institute.Asked where other salts like kosher salt and sea salt fit in, Huang remarked those salts may contain some trace elements “which has those health halos around them, but essentially they’re still primarily sodium chloride.”Huang noted that potassium-enriched salt tastes “about the same as a regular table salt.” She said it’s possible a small number of people with a sensitive palate could taste a difference.

Huang said that “it’s really hard for people to cut back their salt intake.”“But the easier way is just to replace part of the sodium chloride in our normal salt with potassium chloride, because increasing potassium intake also helps to reduce blood pressure,” she said.The two minerals play opposite roles in the body, according to Cheng-Han Chen, MD, a board certified interventional cardiologist and medical director of the Structural Heart Program at MemorialCare Saddleback Medical Center in Laguna Hills, CA. Chen wasn’t involved in the study.

“While sodium causes water retention and increased blood pressure, potassium will help the kidneys remove sodium from the body and lower blood pressure,” Chen told Healthline.Huang mentioned she worked on an earlier trial of about 21,000 people in 600 rural villages in northern China in 2021.

People who used potassium-enriched salt had a 14% lower risk of stroke, a 13% lower risk of cardiovascular events, and a 12% lower risk of early death than those who used regular salt, according to a 2021 study in The New England Journal of Medicine that summarized the trial’s results.

The World Health Organization (WHO) endorsed potassium-enriched salt in a 2025 guideline, saying it can reduce blood pressure and the risk of cardiovascular disease.

The AHA stated potassium-based salt substitutes can help lower blood pressure in some adults. The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued labeling guidance in 2020 allowing an alternate name for potassium chloride on ingredient labels to include the word “salt.”“We think that blood pressure begins to improve as soon as 1 week after cutting back on sodium intake. The full benefit typically takes up to 4 weeks,” Chen said.

Sources indicate that “We generally recommend a daily sodium limit of 2,300 milligrams (mg), ideally under 1,500 mg a day. Most people consume over 3,000 mg of sodium a day, well above the recommended limit,” Chen said.The WHO recommends less than 2,000 mg of sodium per day and suggests at least 3,510 mg of potassium a day.In the United States, more than 70% of salt intake comes from processed and restaurant foods, according to the AHA.

Huang remarked that some people with advanced chronic kidney disease should avoid potassium-enriched salt.When the kidneys don’t work well, the body may not clear extra potassium efficiently, she said. That can lead to hyperkalemia, or high potassium levels in the blood, which can raise the risk of cardiac arrest, Huang said.Among people with stage 3 to stage 5 kidney disease, switching to salt substitutes could prevent about 750,000 deaths a year by lowering blood pressure and cause about 100,000 deaths a year from hyperkalemia, the researchers estimated.The AHA said that people with kidney disease or who take medications that affect potassium should check with a healthcare professional before using these products.

An estimated 37 million U.S. adults have chronic kidney disease, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

Recent findings suggest that potassium-enriched salt is available at supermarkets in the U.S. Many major U.S. grocery chains, including Kroger, Walmart, and Publix, carry two types of products, according to their websites:.

Potassium-enriched salt typically costs about twice as much as regular salt, according to the study.Huang noted she hoped people would see the results and start thinking of the switch as “a simple thing I can do for their own health.”.

Uncontacted Indigenous tribe reaches out for help in the Brazilian Amazon

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (434 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Around the world, the number of uncontacted Indigenous tribes continues to dwindle.
  • It has been revealed that on November 17, the nonprofit advocacy group Survival International reported a recent incident in which 20 members of the Awá people intentionally contacted local government officials in the Brazilian Amazon.
  • “This is a troubling indication of how the continued invasion of uncontacted peoples’ forests puts otherwise self-sufficient Indigenous people in real danger,” Survival International director Caroline Pearce remarked in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Around the world, the number of uncontacted Indigenous tribes continues to dwindle. Indigenous rights advocates estimate that half of the nearly 200 communities still existing in comparative isolation could disappear within a decade, without proper safeguards against climate change, land loss, fame-seeking opportunists, and illegal industrial encroachments. Unfortunately, the situation has apparently grown so dire that some Indigenous groups are reaching out for help—and exposing themselves to potentially deadly foreign diseases in the process.

It has been revealed that on November 17, the nonprofit advocacy group Survival International reported a recent incident in which 20 members of the Awá people intentionally contacted local government officials in the Brazilian Amazon. Although proficient hunter-gatherers, the group requested yams before taking them back into the rainforest.

“This is a troubling indication of how the continued invasion of uncontacted peoples’ forests puts otherwise self-sufficient Indigenous people in real danger,” Survival International director Caroline Pearce remarked in a statement.

The Awá are one of the world’s last uncontacted Indigenous tribes, whose ties to the Brazilian rainforest stretch back centuries. They faced their first attacks from European settlers during the 1800s, which eventually forced them to adopt a nomadic lifestyle to avoid future encounters. Brazil finally supplied the Awá with settlement areas during the mid-1980s, but it still took years before the government properly invested in demarcated land. In the meantime, numerous deadly interactions with loggers, farmers, and other illegal intruders had reduced the Awá community to barely 300 people. Of those, advocates estimate only about one-third of the hunter-gatherers remain completely isolated from the outside world.

“The Brazilian government must commit the resources necessary to protect [the region of] Arariboia from the loggers and ranchers who are razing it, in flagrant defiance of the law,” Pearce added.

Recent findings suggest that in addition to the advocacy work by Survival International, the Awá are supported by a team of Indigenous members of the Guajajara community known as the Forest Guardians. These volunteers have spent years pushing back against illegal cattle ranchers and loggers attempting to claim land in Arariboia, often dying as a result of their efforts.

Industry observers note that “The Forest Guardians have always worked to protect the Awá against encroachment, even at the cost of losing warriors in battle,” the organization mentioned. “We demand immediate action from the relevant authorities…to ensure what the Awá believe is best for them, safeguarding their lives, health, safety and dignity. FOR THE AWÁ, FOR THE TENETEHAR [language], AND FOR THE FOREST!”.

Breaking: The 15 Best Jeans for Men, Tested and Reviewed by Style Editors

📅 22 Aug 2023 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4679 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Menshealth

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, FEW MENSWEAR PIECES nail durability and easy style in one package like a great pair of jeans.
  • It has been revealed that over the past five years, I’ve tested more than 60 pairs across seasons—winter layering, dead-of-summer heat, and everything in between—alongside Men’s Health’s fashion team.
  • The Levi’s 501 is the blueprint of jeans—the one that every other pair takes notes from.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, FEW MENSWEAR PIECES nail durability and easy style in one package like a great pair of jeans. For me, it’s the starting point for most of my outfits. But once you start paying attention, you realize how wide the gap is between pairs that just look good and pairs that can go with a bunch of different looks. Some are so stiff like a straitjacket, others stretch out so much they feel like leggings rather than denim.

It has been revealed that over the past five years, I’ve tested more than 60 pairs across seasons—winter layering, dead-of-summer heat, and everything in between—alongside Men’s Health’s fashion team. We looked at different fits, washes, and cuts across a range of builds and style preferences. Skinny fits are out. Instead, go for relaxed, straight, or straight-slim cuts that fall at the widest part of your legs for a flattering drape.

The Levi’s 501 is the blueprint of jeans—the one that every other pair takes notes from. I’ve had the straight-leg style in my closet for some years now and it fits comfortably every time. It has an easy fit through the hip and thigh, with a slight taper below the knee that doesn’t stack over my shoes. The 501s is made with 100% cotton, that’s sturdy and substantial but still breathable, even in the subway where things feel stuffy.

According to recent reports, levi’s offers five different inseams, which is not standard for most retail denim brands. There’s also plenty of washes and different levels of stretch including low and high stretch as well none at all. In other words, whether you’re tall, short, or somewhere in between, there’s an option for everyone and you can skip wasting money at a tailor. I found that the low-stretch pair gives you enough flex to move around without any stiffness. The no-stretch version broke in nicely after a few wears, and the high-stretch ones felt more laid-back without losing shape, but just a tad less breathable.

I’ve washed the 501s a million times and the fit always held up. It hasn’t become too baggy or too tight. Though I’ve machine dried mine before and only saw minimal shrinkage, I still recommend air drying to keep the fit where it’s at. The button fly took a minute to get used to, but it adds to that vintage feel. Out of all the washes I tried, the medium stonewash was the standout. It’s soft straight out of the box, with just the right amount of fading. It works with everything in my closet: t-shirts and hoodies, oxford shirts and loafers, boots and sneakers.

Read More: How to Wash Your Jeans.

It has been revealed that this pair of travel jeans from Bonobos is the most flexible jean I’ve tested. Honestly, they wear more like athletic pants than traditional denim. The brand uses a stretch cotton blend with a generous dose of elastane, which gives you full range of motion to handle all kinds of airport chaos: twisting and turning through TSA, sprinting to your gate, or squeezing into a tight middle seat.

Industry observers note that I usually fly in sweatpants because I can’t stand feeling restricted on long flights, but these jeans completely changed that. On a 13-hour flight back from Japan, I stayed comfortable the entire time. No pinching, no stiffness, and I wasn’t overheating, either. The fabric is super breathable and lightweight, so even during hot layovers and road trips, I didn’t feel like I was melting.

It has been revealed that another big win: they hold their shape. A lot of high-stretch jeans get that saggy, baggy-knee look after a few hours, but not these. I’ve worn and washed them multiple times, and they still bounce back. And despite the gym-pant-level flexibility, they still look like real jeans; clean, tailored, and polished.

They’re also extremely low-maintenance. I packed them tightly into a carry-on for hours, pulled them out, and didn’t see a single crease. That wrinkle resistance is impressive. They looked crisp and ready to wear, no steamer or iron needed. And in true Bonobos fashion: they come in more waist sizes and fits than just about any brand we’ve tested, so no matter your build, you’ll find a version that works for you.

Abercrombie has one of the strongest takes on the baggy jeans right now. This style of denim in general has fully made its comeback, showing up on runways all the way down to everyday streetwear. The brand’s offering is easy to wear: lightweight, super relaxed through the leg, and has that slight “puddle” at the shoe—meaning the hem stacks a bit over your sneakers instead of hitting right at the ankle.

According to recent reports, I like that it comes in multiple inseams, so you can actually control how much stacking you want depending on your height or how you like your jeans to sit. And with 20-plus colorways, it’s easy to find a version that fits your vibe, whether you want something low-key and neutral or a little more standout. I personally love the vintage black wash that reads clean and modern, even with the looser shape. In terms of fabric, it’s made from 100% cotton that already feels broken-in, so you’re not dealing with anything overly structured out of the gate.

I put on the Ford Standard Jean from Buck Mason, and could instantly feel how durable this pair was. Not only is this denim as tough as they come, it’s built to last and looks damn good doing it. It’s sourced from Japan’s Kaihara mills, which is known for blending traditional shuttle loom techniques with modern innovation. In other words, this fabric has that rich, textured character you expect from premium Japanese denim, but with a level of consistency that ensures long-term durability. At 14 oz, these jeans sit in that sweet spot—not too heavy, not too light—so it feels sturdy but won’t take forever to break in.

Unlike classic 100% cotton, this pair has a hint of stretch that lets me move freely from the jump. The mid-rise sits perfectly at my waist and I noticed the cut is straight through the thighs, giving ample room to breathe and take big, confident strides. If you’ve got some serious quads, that’s not a problem. These jeans can handle your muscles without compromising your style. It tapers neatly down below the knee, laying right on your sneakers for a clean, sharp finish. Whether I’m keeping it casual with a tee or dressing it up with a crisp button-down and blazer, it has that versatile edge to switch things up.

Most selvedge denim is super stiff like cardboard, but that’s not the case with this pair from 3sixteen. Since the cotton fabric blend is infused with a hint of spandex, it's wearable out of the gate. I didn’t go through an annoying break-in period, so I could actually sit down, bike to the bodega, or bend down low without cutting off circulation. The straight fit gives me breathing room instead of feeling painted on. It’s tapered in all the right places so you get that clean, tailored silhouette without feeling like you borrowed your little cousin’s pants. And they’re not stacking weird at the ankle or drowning your sneakers; these sit just right, especially cuffed.

Sources indicate that this is Japanese selvedge denim from Kuroki Mills: a denim mill famed for its high-quality fabrics and innovative production techniques like indigo dyeing. Yes, the pair is priced north of $300, but you get your cost per wear, it goes with a bunch of different looks, and is built to last for years to come.

If you’re the kind of guy who thinks $15 jeans have to feel like cardboard and fit like a punishment, let me introduce you to the Amazon special that exceeds my expectations.These budget jeans clock in at just $15, but they don’t feel like a throwaway buy. The denim is a cotton-elastane blend, so while it’s not that stiff, 100% raw denim people love, it looks like classic denim and feels way more forgiving. That hint of stretch allows me to sit, squat, and climb stairs without any restriction. Honestly, the pair is also comfortable enough to travel in, which is not something I say lightly about most cheap jeans.

It has been revealed that the fabric has a decent weight to it, too. It’s not paper-thin, not overly rigid; just that sweet middle ground that feels broken-in without looking flimsy. Now, are the jeans perfect? No. The zipper jammed on me a couple of times during the first few wears. Not a dealbreaker, because it loosened up and zipped smoothly after a bit, but worth noting. They’re functional, but they don’t have that tank-like durability you’d expect from a $200 pair.

Sources indicate that uniqlo’s straight jeans from its JW Anderson collaboration are a really clean, easy take on everyday denim. It’s got that classic straight-leg silhouette that’s not too baggy or too slim, so it feels wearable right away. I don’t feel like I’m fighting the jeans, but I also don’t feel swallowed by them. One of the standout qualities is the pre-washed finish. You get a subtle, broken-in fade straight out of the box that doesn’t feel stiff or raw.

In a recent development, another thing to note: the inseam is 32, and on me this pair runs a little long, so there’s some stacking at the ankle. I’ve found it looks better cuffed. For taller guys, it creates a nice break over the shoe. When it comes time to style, it pairs nicely with oversized tees, structured outerwear, and pretty much anything you’d wear year-round. This pair just sits well, doesn't feel restrictive, and holds up as a reliable “grab-and-go” pair. Plus, it’s more affordable than most options on the list, meaning you can stock up on the three colorways without blowing too much money.

It has been revealed that when you’re spending good money on denim, it should be built to last and AGOLDE’s jeans fit the bill. The moment I pulled one leg through, I could tell it was rigid yet surprisingly smooth. It’s made from non-stretch sustainable cotton, which breathes well and softens over time without losing structure. It also has some heft, so I wouldn’t wear it in high-80- or 90-degree temps, but I’ll be reaching for it from fall straight through spring.

According to recent reports, style-wise, it’s a nice departure from your classic blue denim, with a washed-out grey hue that looks sharp with a plain tee or lightweight flannel and boots. My only gripe is the fit: the jeans are already baggy and only come in a 32-inch inseam, which creates more stacking than I’d like at 5 '8". I had mine hemmed slightly to clean up the break. If you’re 5 ‘11” or taller, though, it’ll drape over your shoes or boots the way it’s intended without looking overly bunched.

Sources indicate that if you’re looking to lean into the Western workwear trend without going full cowboy, AG’s classic bootcut Jean is an easy place to start. I wore this pair to the Beyonce Cowboy Carter concert to coincide with the album’s theme, but it also works just as well for everyday wear when you want to keep things more understated. For the office, you could wear it with a crisp button-down, simple tee, and minimal sneakers. From a fabric standpoint, the cotton-elastane blend has enough give to move with you, while the premium stretch denim from Japan’s renowned Kaihara mill still feels substantial.

Industry observers note that it tapered through the thigh before opening slightly below the knee and sits naturally over cowboy boots. Though it looks just as sharp with clean leather sneakers if boots aren’t your thing. AG only offers one color, but I love the medium-blue wash, which has a clean, lived-in look that adds character without looking overly faded, making it easy to dress up or down. I’d throw it on with a plain white tee and overshirt for the weekend or a denim shirt and leather boots when I want to lean into that classic Americana vibe. Like AGOLDE’s jeans, this pair also only comes in a 32-inch inseam. In this case, it works for guys who are closer to 5’11” or taller.

Wrangler makes one of the most iconic cowboy jeans out there for decades. These were originally made for working cowboys and riders, but this timeless silhouette works for a casual office day or weekend outings. The denim is heavyweight cotton, so right away you feel that structure with a broken-in-over-time feel.

Sources indicate that fit-wise, it sits higher on the waist and runs straight through the leg with room where you actually need it—seat and thigh especially. That’s why guys with thicker legs tend to gravitate toward them. They don’t squeeze you or taper too hard, so you actually get comfort without losing that classic straight-leg Western shape. It’s not chasing trends or trying to be “updated.” And if you’re looking for a more affordable alternative to the AG Jeans, this is your best bet.

Sources indicate that brooks Brothers may be known for Oxford shirts and chinos, but our fashion editors were thoroughly impressed by the Americana brand’s denim. Its slim fit pair is made with premium, mid-weight denim that’s super robust, but soft enough to wear for hours, with a hint of spandex for extra mobility. The fit is where the pair truly shine—a precise, tailored cut that contours through the hips and thighs for a clean silhouette without being super tight. Although the jeans fit closer to the body, you don’t feel like you’re suffocating.

Every stitch is strategically placed, reflecting Brooks Brothers’ heritage in classic menswear while still feeling fresh and contemporary. Style-wise, these jeans bridge the gap between smart-casual and laid-back cool, so we’ve worn them to a baseball game as well as an office meeting. These jeans are a dream for a lean to moderately athletic build, though if you have a muscular lower body, you might want to size up.

Recent findings suggest that I’ve probably tested over 30 pairs of dark wash jeans in the past few years, and they all start to blur together. But I can confirm that this one from Tommy Hilfiger is an exception. The straight cut is what really sold me. Because it’s regular from the hip to the hem, it doesn’t pinch when I sit down. You know that awful feeling when you’re at your desk or on the train and your jeans dig into your hips like a vice grip? None of that here. I wore these straight through a long shoot day and a subway ride home without needing to unbutton them the second I walked in the door.

In a recent development, the fabric blend is another win: it’s mostly cotton with a hit of lyocell. That synthetic blend softens things up in a way pure cotton denim never does. It almost feels broken-in right off the rack but still has the structure of a good pair of jeans. And unlike stretch-heavy blends, it doesn’t bag out or sag. The deep rich indigo wash makes it easy to dress things up with a blazer, but casual enough that I can throw on sneakers and a simple tee without it looking too forced.

Industry observers note that our style editors did some research and it turns out that there is no rule saying you can only wear white denim during the summer. Every guy could use a pair in their wardrobe, and make good use of it all year around. The best option we found is this pair from Ralph Lauren that has a pearly white texture, while providing the rugged comfort of a pair of jeans. It’s a straight fit but not too loose, and there was just a hint of stretch for a little boost in comfort.

According to recent reports, if you haven’t worn white denim in the past because you’re just not sure how to style it, the trick is to think of something you already know how to work with and just switch this jean in. If you wear chinos in any shade of khaki or brown, a pair of white jeans will give an edgier look without having to change anything else about the outfit. You get the opposite effect when it comes to bluejeans, where swapping them for white elevates the feel of, what is otherwise, the same outfit.

The fit of a black jean is crucial to pulling off dressed up fit, and that is exactly what Lee did here. For starters, I’m 5’8 and the slim-straight cut elongates my profile, giving a sleek, balanced silhouette. This pair is tailored to hug my frame just right without feeling like I squeezed into skinny jeans. When wearing them out on multiple occasions, I still felt like I had enough room to move, thanks to the comforting stretch fabric.

Adorned with branded hardware and the leather logo patch, the aesthetic feels like a nod to the past, while the modern cut still keeps you looking fresh. In terms of style, this pair is the ultimate wardrobe chameleon, working in both casual and semi-dressy settings. It looked just as great with a simple tee and sneakers at a backyard BBQ, as it did with a sport coat and dress shoes at a theater show.

Recent findings suggest that indigo is the dye that makes most jeans blue. When a brand uses a really rich indigo, like Mavi did here, you get a beautiful range from deep, dark navy and light sky blue. The lighter fades gradually show up and get more pronounced with each wear in a jean like this.

Sources indicate that mavi nailed the modern athletic fit in this jean, providing plenty of room in the hip and thigh, along with a taper in the lower leg that looks clean and stylish. This fit is assisted by a blend of cotton, tencel, polyester, and elastane that is lightweight and stretchy. It was one of the most comfortable jeans for our testers with big quads.

It has been revealed that the right fit is the foundation of great jeans. A well-fitting pair should flatter your body type, feel comfortable, and align with your personal style. Here's a breakdown of common fits:.

A slim fit jean is slightly tapered from the thigh to the ankle for a modern, streamlined silhouette. It's great for lean, athletic, or average builds who want a sleek, put-together look. Not to get them confused with skinny jeans, they're not nearly as tight, but they are more form-fitting than straight-leg jeans. Because slim fit jeans are so sleek, they pair well with everything—tees, button-downs, and even blazers. In terms of footwear, it can be worn with dress shoes or sneakers.

A straight fit has a uniform width from hip to hem, meaning no tapering at the ankle. It works for all body types, and offers a relaxed but structured look. Offering a balanced silhouette that isn't too baggy or too tight, this fit works great for everyday wear, whether you're pairing it with a flannel, sweatshirt, or polo shirt.

Industry observers note that A relaxed cut has extra room in the seat, thighs, and leg, so it’s the most comfortable fit, but it also gives laid-back that’s come back in style. It's ideal for bigger guys, muscular legs, and more breathability. We found it looks great with oversized or relaxed tops to maintain proportion.

A tapered cut is slightly wider in the thighs and gradually narrow toward the ankle. It's a sweet spot between straight-leg and slim-fit jeans—giving you some comfort up top while keeping things clean and tailored below. Ideal for guys with athletic thighs or anyone who wants a streamlined look without going full-blown skinny.

Elastane and spandex (same thing, just different names) are synthetic fibers known for thor serious stretch and bounce-back ability. They’re the secret sauce in modern jeans that makes them way comfier than the stiff, unyielding denim of decades past. A bit of elastane—usually around 1-2%— gives jeans just enough flex to move with you, making them ideal for guys who blueprint to wear their jeans all day everyday, whether that’s sitting at a desk, running errands, or just kicking back. The trade-off? Stretchy jeans don’t always hold their shape as well as OG 100% cotton denim.

Sources indicate that no stretch, no shortcuts. At first, these jeans are stiff. But over time, they mold to your body, creating a custom fit. If you love the idea of breaking in a pair like a well-worn leather jacket, go for this kind—but be ready for a couple uncomfortable weeks.

Industry observers note that the holy grail for denim lovers. Selvedge denim is considered top-tier because of its durability, excellent craftsmanship, and the way it develops over time. It’s woven on old-school shuttle looms, which produces a fancy self-finished edge inside the cuff. This means the fabric is denser, less prone to fraying, and typically of higher-quality than mass-produced denim. The real magic? It molds to your body and fades in a way that’s totally unique to how you wear them—no fake distressing needed. The downside? It’s usually stiff at first. Since most selvedge denim is raw (aka unwashed), it starts out rigid, like a thick cotton canvas—but, in the end, it rewards you with some of the best-looking, long-lasting jeans out there.

Your inseam isn't just a number—it dictates whether your jeans stack, skim, or flood. If your denim is too short—you're in capri territory, unless you're purposely rocking cropped jeans. If they're too long, we hope you like puddles of denim at your ankles. For that just-right length, your jeans should either break (gently touch the top of your shoes) or stack naturally if that's your thing.

According to recent reports, most brands offer 30", 32", and 34" inseams, but if you're a shorter or taller guy, look for brands that offer extended sizing or hemming services (Uniqlo and Levi's are great for this). Pro tip: If you like cuffing, go a little longer. If you want a clean, straight-down look, hem them or buy your exact length.

When it comes to denim type in terms of wash and color, you’re choosing between raw vs. washed and light vs. dark vs. everything in between. The right pick depends on how much patience you have, how polished you want to look, and whether you mind a little indigo rub-off. Here’s the breakdown:.

This is denim in its purest form: untouched, unwashed, and dark as midnight. It starts out stiff and gradually fades in all the right places based on how you wear them. The trade-off? It takes commitment—you’ll need to break them in, and they might stain your lighter clothes and furniture (hello, indigo bleed).

Pre-washed for softness and color variation, so you get that broken-in look without the break-in period. If you want instant comfort and zero dye transfer, this is your move. If personal fades is your jam, go raw. As for a consistent color and softness from day one, go washed.

In a recent development, the most versatile option—dress it up with a blazer or down with a hoodie. Darker washes are slimming and work in almost any setting. Raw or rinse denim will develop natural fades over time, adding character.

A casual, everyday wash that looks good with everything. Already has some fading, so there’s no awkward stiff phase. Think of it as the sweet spot between too dressy and too relaxed.

Laid-back, retro, and effortlessly cool—perfect for summer or a more relaxed vibe. Looks great with white tees, sneakers, and vintage-inspired fits. Not as dressy as dark denim, but adds character to your wardrobe.

Since 2021, myself and the Men's Health style team have gone full denim detective mode—testing more than 50 different pairs, each worn for at least two weeks at a time, and six hours a day. As someone who’s 5"8" and typically wears 28W/30L, I know what works and what doesn’t. I threw these jeans into every case scenario—casual brunches, city commutes, long-haul flights, running errands, and yes, even squatting for good measure. I took detailed notes on fit, comfort, wash, inseam, and performance (stretch, moisture-wicking, breathability).We checked if they were true to size, how the fabric held up through hours of movement, whether they needed a marathon break-in, and if they could work in a variety of settings. Our testers also include a diverse range of body types to help us ensure an unbiased result for selecting the best jeans for men. We made sure our picks weren’t trendy jeans, but true workhorses that will look great years from now.

Sources indicate that as the most versatile article of clothing a man can own, jeans have the ability to traverse many different types of formality. Given that denim originates from workwear, it inherently embodies a casual nature. That's why I suggest throwing in some contrast, like rocking penny loafers with laid-back tailoring.

Industry observers note that for a more laid-back look, pair your jeans with a well-fitted tee and canvas or leather sneakers. But when aiming for a smarter appearance, combining dark wash jeans with a crisp button-down shirt or sweater with a pair of boots is a great idea as well.

According to recent reports, on the other hand, for a business casual look, throw on a pair of suede loafers with dark denim, an oxford button down, and timeless accessories. Take those same jeans and style your denim with a pair of low-top sneakers like common projects white sneakers, or a heavyweight crewneck sweatshirt and you've got a great weekend look for fall.

100% cotton denim will feel sturdier and often lasts longer—but it can be stiff at first. A cotton-elastane blend adds comfort and mobility. Neither is “better” universally; it depends on how you wear your jeans. If you’re commuting, traveling, or sitting all day, stretch will keep you comfortable. If you want that old-school fade-and-mold-to-your-body experience, go full cotton.

In a recent development, look at the stitching. Tight, even seams with no loose threads means you have a pair of durable jeans. Check the rivets (those little metal reinforcements at pocket corners), the zipper glide, and the heft of the waist button. Quality jeans often have reinforced belt loops and sturdy pocket bags that don’t feel like tissue paper.

Recent findings suggest that think about silhouette. The rise—whether high, mid, or low—changes where the jeans sit on your torso and can subtly shift proportions. From there, it’s about the leg shape. Straight-leg jeans are timeless and work on nearly everyone. Tapered cuts offer more room in the thigh with a slimmer opening at the ankle, ideal if you lift or prefer a cleaner line. Slim fits narrow throughout for a sharper look, while flares and bootcuts widen at the hem and are designed to sit neatly over boots (and yes, they’re creeping back into the mainstream). The right combination of rise and fit can make an affordable pair look elevated—or make an expensive pair look completely wrong.

Juiced Scrambler Mini debuted as a cooler (and safer) e-bike option for teens and parents

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, finding an electric bike for a teenager can be surprisingly tricky.
  • The newly launched Juiced Scrambler Mini looks like it could do a pretty good job of threading that needle.
  • The new youth-sized e-bike takes the mini-motorcycle styling of Juiced’s larger Scrambler models and shrinks it down around 16-inch fat tires, creating a bike designed for riders between 4’0″ and 5’3″ (122 to 160 cm).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, finding an electric bike for a teenager can be surprisingly tricky. Parents generally want something safe, manageable, and from a reputable company. Teenagers, meanwhile, generally want something that doesn’t look like it was picked out by their parents.

The newly launched Juiced Scrambler Mini looks like it could do a pretty good job of threading that needle.

The new youth-sized e-bike takes the mini-motorcycle styling of Juiced’s larger Scrambler models and shrinks it down around 16-inch fat tires, creating a bike designed for riders between 4’0″ and 5’3″ (122 to 160 cm). But perhaps more importantly for parents, Juiced also built in a PIN-protected speed limiter known as Speed Lock that lets adults decide just how fast the bike can go.

Recent findings suggest that the Scrambler Mini ships set to a 10 mph (16 km/h) Beginner Mode, but its maximum speed can be adjusted anywhere from 1-20 mph (32 km/h) and then locked behind a four-digit PIN. Juiced notes that riders aged 8-12 should not exceed 10 mph, while riders 13 and older can use the bike at speeds up to 20 mph, subject of course to local laws and regulations. In almost every state and jurisdiction though, the bike will fit Class 2 designation for street-legal riding and bike lane operation.

Industry observers note that that setup seems like a pretty smart way to approach youth e-bikes. Instead of buying a slow bike that a teenager may quickly outgrow – or handing them a much faster machine before a parent thinks they’re ready – the same bike can essentially grow with the rider (with speed titrated by a parent or guardian).

And from the kid’s perspective, it certainly doesn’t look like a safety-first children’s bike.

The Scrambler Mini gets the same sort of moto-inspired styling that has defined Juiced’s Scrambler lineup, including a long bench seat, dual-crown-style fork, chunky 16 x 4-inch tires, and several appropriately loud color options including Blackberry, Fruit Punch, Blueberry, and Pink Lemonade.

There’s some decent hardware underneath that styling, too. The rear hub motor is rated at 500W nominal and 1,092W peak with 80 Nm of torque. A removable 48V 10Ah battery using LG cells provides 480Wh of capacity, with Juiced claiming up to 40 miles (64 km) of range. Four levels of cadence-based pedal assist are included, as is a right-side thumb throttle.

It has been revealed that the bike also features Talon hydraulic disc brakes with large 180mm rotors front and rear, 50mm of front suspension travel, an integrated backlit LCD, a headlight, and a rear taillight with brake-light functionality. The single-speed bike weighs 59 lb (26.8 kg), has a 27.15-inch seat height, and is rated for up to 275 lb (125 kg) of payload.

Those parts are far above what we normally see on e-bikes targeted towards teens, with most teen-focused e-bikes sporting cheaper components like mechanical brakes and rigid forks.

In a recent development, the Scrambler Mini is listed at $1,099, though Juiced is currently offering a Black Friday sale that drops the price by another $150 to just $949. The company says preorders are expected to begin shipping the week of December 7.

That price also comes with something increasingly vital in the crowded youth e-bike market: an actual firm standing behind the bike. Juiced was founded in 2009, rapidly becoming a leader in the market for powerful and stylish e-bikes. But after the brand’s financial troubles a few years ago, Lectric eBikes stepped in to take Juiced under its wing in 2025. The relaunched Juiced now offers a three-year manufacturer warranty and US-based support, plus the peace of mind that comes with backing from North America’s largest e-bike company, Lectric eBikes.

That last part may be just as appealing to parents as the speed limiter, though the 3-year warranty is definitely a deal sweetener, too.

There’s always going to be some controversy around the idea of e-bikes marketed towards teens, but I’m for it when done responsibly. Let’s face it: e-bikes are incredibly popular and teens are already going to be riding them, even if it means borrowing a friend’s e-bike because they don’t have their own. So if they’re going to be riding, the least we can do is put them on a safer, higher-quality bike so they learn the right skills in the right environment. And hey, it sure beats teens sitting alone in their rooms texting each other all afternoon.

When it comes to choosing an e-bike, there are already plenty of cheap mini e-bikes and electric dirt bike-style machines floating around online, and many are undoubtedly going to look tempting to teenagers. The Scrambler Mini seems to take a different approach, giving young riders the styling, fat tires, throttle, and mini-moto attitude they actually want, while giving parents control over how much of that performance they can access.

Sources indicate that it’s still an e-bike capable of 20 mph, and that means parents need to make decisions about where, when, and how their kids ride it. And there’s even an argument to be made for removing the throttle and turning it into a Class 1 e-bike in the beginning, requiring a teen to pedal it to engage the motor. But I’d much rather see that conversation happening around a bike with hydraulic brakes, lights, a programmable speed limit, and a real organization standing behind it than around some anonymous electric mini-bike bought from the depths of the internet.

And if the teenager thinks it looks cool enough to actually ride, that’s probably the point.
