#166919. How to Survive the Holidays With "Ignorant" Relatives

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (754 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

How to Survive the Holidays With "Ignorant" Relatives

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (754 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Updated November 23, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.
  • One phrase that changed my life forever is: "The map is not the territory.".
  • According to recent reports, there is a reality out there—the territory—but our only way to access it is through the representations of it we create and carry around in our heads.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Updated November 23, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.

One phrase that changed my life forever is: "The map is not the territory.".

According to recent reports, there is a reality out there—the territory—but our only way to access it is through the representations of it we create and carry around in our heads. These are our maps. And every human being has a slightly different map. When I say "red," and you imagine red, how can we be certain we're imagining the same hue, tint, etc.? We can't.

So, we arrive at a dining table this holiday season convinced that our opinions simply describe what any reasonable and rational person would see when they looked at the world... the facts... the territory. Naturally, a relative who disagrees with our map must be missing some vital information, or be lacking in the intelligence needed to process that information correctly, or both. We think that they are ignorant; if they only had a map as good as ours, they would agree with us.

In Role Mate to Soul Mate, relationship expert Warren Farrell writes that certainty can close us off to other people’s perspectives. His chapter “From Civil War to Civil Dialogue” offers tools for staying in conversation when disagreements get heated.

According to recent reports, farrell recommends preparing before the meal. Start with “nemesis visualization”: Picture the relative who interrupts, misunderstands you, or repeats their point more loudly. The goal isn’t to rehearse a fight. It’s to let go of the hope that this time you’ll finally change their mind and choose peace instead.

Another tool is “Alone Power”: the ability, on your own, to help another person feel heard. That doesn’t mean agreeing. It means listening closely enough that the other person can see that you are truly trying to understand them. Holiday dinners put this skill to the test; we may say we want less division, while quietly hoping everyone will come around to our view. First, we need to know how to make other people feel heard.

Recent findings suggest that next, think of a few qualities you genuinely respect in that relative and recognize in yourself. Farrell calls attention to three possible points of common ground: caring, curiosity, and courage (the three Cs). You might not share all three, and that’s fine. Choose what resonates with you. Finding one shared quality can make it easier to stay curious about the person beneath the argument.

It has been revealed that when the conversation starts to escalate, notice whether you’re already composing your rebuttal. Silently say “hold” to yourself, and then take a deep breath or recall something beautiful that helps you feel grounded. Try these three steps:.

Keep checking until the other person feels accurately understood.

Feeling heard often reduces someone’s need to keep arguing, so use the holidays to practice your active listening skills.

This is my favorite exercise. Farrell’s premise is that a virtue, pushed to an extreme, can become a vice. The exercise asks you to look for the value inside an opinion that irritates you. In his example, a conservative father and liberal daughter discover shared values beneath their political disagreement, including compassion, equality of opportunity, and self-respect. From there, they can replace proselytizing with a search for mutual solutions.

According to recent reports, we don’t have to abandon our convictions or pretend to agree with our relatives; we simply have to become sufficiently curious to inquire why the maps in their heads are so different from the maps in ours. We can ask what matters to them, and if the conversation becomes disrespectful or frustrating, we can set a limit: “I care about you, but I don’t want to keep arguing about this. Let’s talk about something else.”.

We have to be the change we want to see in the world. Imagine how much more peaceful the world would be if we all remembered that the map is not the territory. We would waste less time believing that other people are ignorant and spend more time becoming curious about their maps. At the end of the day, everyone just wants to feel heard, seen, respected... loved. Maybe a more harmonious, compassionate, and less polarized world starts at your dining room table this holiday season.

Farrell, W. (2024). Role Mate to Soul Mate: The Seven Secrets to Lifelong Love. BenBella Books.

The free-to-play game set in the the universe of Arknights has been in various forms of closed tests for a while, but it finally has a release date.

The game is set to arrive simultaneously across PC, PS5, and mobile (iOS, Android) on January 22, and pre-registrations continue to be open.

Sources indicate that gryphline broke the news on The Game Awards stage alongside a chunky trailer featuring a new OneRepublic song. It actually ends up being a nice tone piece for the world of Arknights, showing a lot of cinematics alongside the music itself.

It has been revealed that the developer-publisher also declared that so far, Arknights: Endfield has had over 30 million pre-registrations worldwide since pre-registrations went live. Some players have been able to play early, of course, with the most recent opportunity being Beta Test 2.

If you’ve been following the game’s development, you’ll know that it was pretty clear we’re closer than ever to the official launch. The most recent beta build showed off polished content, with fresh animations and cutscenes.

We’ve been playing it ourselves, and we think you’re going to agree with our Arknights: Endfield character tier list. You can expect more coverage from us as we get closer to launch, and when the game actually arrives.

Though it might seem like it came out of nowhere, the game is based on the Arknights universe, itself a massive mobile game with over 100 million downloads. Endfield brings a different flavour to that world, with a mix of strategy, exploration and real-time combat, not unlike the many games created by HoYoverse.

You can pre-register yourself on the official website.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that tesla has opened its first Semi Megacharger in Texas, an 8-stall station in Mesquite on the east side of Dallas. With it, Tesla’s map now lists 7 public Megacharger sites and 44 stalls for its electric truck.

That’s progress. But with six weeks left in 2026, it’s less than a fifth of the 37 sites Tesla planned to have open this year.

Tesla Charging announced the newly introduced station on X on Tuesday night with its usual one-liner and a photo of the stalls at sunset:.

New Tesla Megacharger: Mesquite, TX (8 stalls) https://t.co/UsCFMyCjo7 pic.twitter.com/W4G1e2BHkb.

Tesla’s map lists the site at 2175 S Town East Blvd in Mesquite, with eight Megachargers rated at up to 1.2 MW each.

Industry observers note that texas is where Tesla has the most riding on this network. When Tesla added 64 Megacharger locations to its map in February, Texas got 19 of the 66 planned sites, more than any other state. Mesquite is the first of them to go live, and several other Dallas–Fort Worth sites are still marked “coming soon.”.

The Pilot truck stop rollout hasn’t reached Texas either. When Pilot opened its first Megacharger in Georgia in October, it named a Flying J in Fort Stockton, Texas, as one of the next sites. It’s still not live on Tesla’s map.

It has been revealed that tesla also isn’t alone in DFW. Greenlane, the truck charging joint venture between Daimler Truck, NextEra and BlackRock, announced high-power sites in Dallas and Houston in May, open to any electric truck with CCS and MCS connectors. Tesla now has a station operating in the metro.

Here’s every public Megacharger currently live on Tesla’s map:.

In a recent development, that’s 7 sites and 44 stalls in four states. When we counted in early October, there were four customer-facing sites with 26 stalls. Tulare opened the same week, Hodgkins came on November 10, and now Mesquite.

So Tesla is adding a site roughly every two weeks.

Tesla also runs private Megachargers for its own fleet at Giga Nevada and in Carson, California, and it sells Megachargers to fleets and depot operators through its business program. Forum Mobility switched on two at the Port of Long Beach earlier this month. None of those count toward the public network that Semi buyers without their own depot rely on.

Sources indicate that tesla’s Q4 2025 shareholder report highlighted about 37 Megacharger sites for 2026. Semi program lead Dan Priestley has remarked Tesla wants 46 by early 2027.

To me this seems like good progress, sure it's not right on time with their ambitious goal, but they are executing on their charging network and I'm sure more sites will keep opening.

It has been revealed that to hit 37, Tesla would need to open 30 more sites in the next 43 days. At the current pace, it ends the year with around 10.

It has been revealed that pilot mentioned in October that nine more of its sites were under construction, so a late burst is possible. But it would have to be a very big one.

According to recent reports, and the trucks are starting to show up. Tesla debuted volume production of the Semi in September at a Nevada factory it says can build 50,000 trucks a year, and it stated last week that Chicago’s first 50 Semis are en route for delivery, a day after Hodgkins opened. Big fleets like that customer are installing their own depot chargers anyway, and most Semi charging will happen there. The public network is what lets a Semi leave its home region.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that amflow has made a name for itself in the electric mountain bike world with its high-performance Avinox-powered machines, but now the tech giant is bringing that same technology to a decidedly more urban environment. The newly unveiled Amflow UE Carbon series marks the brand’s first move into the commuter e-bike market, combining a lightweight carbon fiber frame, powerful mid-drive motor, and a surprisingly long list of smart features designed for everyday riding.

And while these might look like fairly conventional step-through city bikes at first glance, there’s some seriously impressive technology hiding beneath those clean lines.

The new Amflow UE series comes in two versions, the UE Carbon and the higher-end UE Carbon Pro, both built around a full-carbon fiber frame weighing just 2.35 kg (5.2 lb).

The complete bike weighs as little as 20.9 kg (46 lb), which is fairly impressive considering the amount of hardware Amflow has packed into it, including front suspension, a suspension dropper seatpost, integrated lighting, and cargo racks.

According to recent reports, both models use the Avinox M2 mid-drive motor, which delivers up to 125 Nm of torque. That’s an enormous amount of torque for a city bike, and should make short work of steep hills, especially when carrying groceries or other cargo. And to put things into perspective, a lot of city e-bikes have barely 60 Nm for torque, so Amflow is knocking it out of the park for urban power.

A removable 600 Wh battery provides a claimed maximum range of 132 km (82 miles) in the lowest power assist mode, while fast charging can refill the battery in just 2 hours and 23 minutes.

The bikes also feature Avinox’s intelligent traction control system and a upcoming Auto Boost function that automatically provides additional assistance when the system detects demanding conditions, such as accelerating from a stop or climbing a steep hill.

In other words, riders get much of the sophisticated motor technology developed for high-performance electric mountain bikes, but in a package designed for commuting to work or picking up groceries.

Industry observers note that the bike is listed as weighing 20.9 kg (46 lb), though that figure conveniently excludes the front and rear racks, mudguards, pedals, kickstand, bike lock, bottle cage, and chainguard. So figure a few extra pounds for all of that gear, and you’re in the right ballpark.

The main difference between the two models is their drivetrain.

The higher-end UE Carbon Pro ($3,899) uses a customized three-speed electronically shifted internally geared hub paired with a Gates carbon belt drive. That should make it particularly appealing to commuters who want a quiet, clean, low-maintenance setup without worrying about chain lubrication or derailleur adjustments.

The more affordable UE Carbon ($3,499) instead uses a 10-speed electronic derailleur developed with TRP.

Both models support automatic shifting, allowing the bike to handle gear changes without requiring the rider to constantly think about them.

Amflow has also gone fairly wild with the technology integration.

There’s a 1.4-inch touchscreen display mounted on the handlebars, a wireless phone charging mount offering 15W wireless charging or 20W USB-C charging, and integrated lighting with automatic low-light activation and brake-sensing functionality.

The bikes even include a hardened steel frame lock on the rear wheel, Apple Find My integration, and a Lost Mode feature that can lock down certain components if the bike is stolen.

Apple Watch connectivity allows riders to check their bike’s status and unlock it, while heart-rate-based assistance can automatically adjust motor output to help riders maintain a target heart rate zone.

Some of these features, like the security and tracking, are immediately effective for nearly all riders, while other high-tech features like the heart rate-based pedal assist can provide even more functionality for niche riders looking to bridge the gap between riding for transportation and riding for fitness.

Of course, all the fancy technology in the world doesn’t mean much if a commuter bike can’t handle everyday errands.

Fortunately, Amflow appears to have taken the practical side seriously.

The bikes feature a low step-through frame, upright riding position, 65 mm suspension fork, and a suspension dropper seatpost offering 125 mm of height adjustment and approximately 30 mm of suspension travel.

The 26×2.0-inch Maxxis tires should also provide a comfortable ride over less-than-perfect city streets.

There’s a front rack rated for 20 kg (44 lb) and a rear rack rated for 27 kg (59.5 lb), with the latter supporting the MIK HD mounting system for compatible accessories, including child seats.

The standard frame is designed to accommodate riders from 155 to 190 cm (5’1” to 6’3”), while a smaller version for riders down to 140 cm (4’7”) is expected in 2027.

I’ve been impressed with the technology coming out of the Avinox ecosystem, and it’s exciting to see that technology finally make its way into a more practical city-focused electric bicycle.

According to recent reports, as much as I love high-performance electric mountain bikes, the reality is that most people aren’t spending their mornings bombing down mountain trails. They’re commuting to work, dropping kids off at school, and running errands.

And that’s where electric bicycles can make an even bigger difference.

It has been revealed that the Amflow UE series seems to take a refreshingly comprehensive approach to urban riding. The powerful motor is nice, but I’m arguably more interested in the belt drive, integrated security, cargo capacity, automatic shifting, and built-in phone charging.

It has been revealed that those are the kinds of features that can make an electric bicycle genuinely easier to live with every day. And as someone who actually commutes with an e-bike each day as my main form of transportation, these bikes are really speaking to me!

Recent findings suggest that if you ask me, it’s great to see another high-performance e-bike manufacturer recognizing that the future of electric bicycles isn’t just about riding farther and faster on trails. It’s also about making everyday transportation better for the less exciting type of riding, too.

Lord of Hatred delivers a new campaign that continues the mainline story, picking up from where Vessel of Hatred left off. Mephisto, the eponymous Lord of Hatred, has seemingly finally escaped imprisonment to rule over Sanctuary.

Lord of Hatred is the second Diablo 4 expansion, and it will be available on PC, PS5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S on April 28.

It’s always a significant deal when we get a newly introduced Diablo expansion, especially for a game as starved of fresh (major) content as Diablo 4 has been. But perhaps the biggest piece of news out of the Lord of Hatred reveal is that the expansion is bringing not one, but two new classes to the game.

The first of which is The Paladin, whereas the second is being kept under wraps. Even more surprising is that The Paladin is playable right now for anyone who pre-purchases the expansion. This is a well-timed shadow drop, especially given that Diablo 4’s latest season has just kicked off.

Sources indicate that the expansion adds a latest region to the world: Skovos, which is where the events of the new campaign will be taking place. This is the first time Skovos has been in a Diablo game. The region is of major significance to the world and lore of the series, as it is the birthplace of the firstborn, home of Lilith and Inaruis.

Lord of Hatred brings a decent number of major systems to Diablo 4. The endgame is getting a major overhaul, headlined by the new War Aims feature. Through this, you can effectively design your own endgame grind, creating challenges based on the activities you like and earning rewards along the way.

Endgame activities now also feature their own skill trees, which can be progressed through by creating War Plans for your character featuring each activity. The latest endgame activity, Echoing Hatred, is something of horde mode where you must defend against unrelenting waves of enemies.

None of that matters without loot, of course, and the upcoming expansion is bringing back the Horadric Cube, and adding set bonuses using the Talisman system. The long-awaited and highly-requested Loot Filter is also coming to the game with the release of the expansion.

It has been revealed that beyond itemisation, each class’ skill tree will grow with newly introduced bonus skill variants. In fact, the entire skill system is being reworked for all classes - though details are a little sparse at the moment.

Industry observers note that you can also expect the level cap to go up, which is very likely necessary to fit all the new skills and various systems. Blizzard offered a deep dive into the new Paladin class, which you see on the official blog.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, how do you get more out of a battery without adding weight or more cells?
  • Unlike traditional lithium-ion, LFP batteries use no nickel or cobalt, which helps reduce costs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ford has entered the battery business. The first LFP battery cells are now rolling off the assembly line at Ford’s BlueOval Battery Park plant in Michigan and are headed to power Fathom prototypes in Kentucky.

In a recent development, how do you get more out of a battery without adding weight or more cells? According to Alan Clarke, Ford’s vice president of advanced development projects, who is also leading its Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform, the answer lies in lithium iron phosphate (LFP) technology.

Unlike traditional lithium-ion, LFP batteries use no nickel or cobalt, which helps reduce costs. They also typically hold up better after years of use and charging.

Sources indicate that to make it a reality, Ford turned to CATL, the leading global EV battery manufacturer. Ford uses CATL’s licensed technology and manufacturing expertise at its BlueOval Battery Park Michigan plant.

Ford said it will be the first in the US to deliver LFP batteries for mainstream automotive use, with the battery cells now rolling off the line in Michigan.

The first LFP battery cells are headed to Ford’s Louisville Assembly Plant and will be used to power Fathom prototypes, its first vehicle based on the UEV platform.

Recent findings suggest that ford designed and engineered the Fathom from the ground up for efficiency. As such, it chose prismatic battery cells because they fit directly into the chassis, reducing structural costs.

With cells now being delivered from a plant that it owns and operates, Ford said it will use the knowledge gained in Michigan to support more affordable EVs and Ford Energy, its upcoming battery energy storage business in Kentucky.

At Ford’s new battery plant in Michigan, assembly lines can deliver 40 cells every minute, making it one of the fastest LFP prismatic battery assembly lines outside China.

Although the accelerated output drives down costs, Ford noted employees use AI-powered image recognition and inspection tools to spot defects in real time and maintain quality.

“Our goal is to make defective cells so rare that we track their frequency per billion cells rather than per million,” Ford said.

With production testing now underway, Ford intends to have the battery pack plant in Michigan up and running in 2027, ahead of schedule.

Ford will open preorders for the Fathom in early 2027, starting at $28,350 for the standard-range model.

CEO Jim Farley noted on the company’s third-quarter earnings call last month that the Fathom, Ford’s first vehicle based on the UEV platform, remains on track to launch in Q4 2027.

Farley said the Fathom is a “breakthrough product” that’s highly capable and still affordable. The starting MSRP is under $30,000, and the low cost of ownership is perfect for today’s market, he added.

Industry observers note that ford and Slate both producing vehicles with US-produced LFP batteries is a great milestone. Hopefully we can keep pushing our domestic battery supply chain forward.

Ford said the Fathom will offer more interior space than a Toyota RAV4, and it will cost less to own over five years than a three-year-old used Tesla Model Y.

The pickup will be the first vehicle to integrate Apple Maps directly into the navigation system. All versions will be BlueCruise-capable for hands-free driving, with standard Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, plus bidirectional charging capabilities.

Although we have yet to see it, Ford stated the Fathom features a “large touchscreen display” with easy-to-use navigation.

Ford has not revealed battery specs or range, but we do know the pickup will have an NACS port after several prototypes were spotted at a Tesla Supercharger over the summer.

#166909. How Professionals May Overlook Intrafamilial Child Torture

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1438 w)

How Professionals May Overlook Intrafamilial Child Torture

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1438 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 23, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.
  • Industry observers note that coauthored with Pamela J.
  • Recent findings suggest that intrafamilial child torture (“ICT”) usually involves a combination of physical, sexual, and psychological abuse, and intentional neglect, of a child, that is 1) severe and egregious, 2) prolonged without intervention, and 3) deliberate on the part of the offending parent (Miller, et al, 2021).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 23, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.

Industry observers note that coauthored with Pamela J. Miller, JD., MSW.

Recent findings suggest that intrafamilial child torture (“ICT”) usually involves a combination of physical, sexual, and psychological abuse, and intentional neglect, of a child, that is 1) severe and egregious, 2) prolonged without intervention, and 3) deliberate on the part of the offending parent (Miller, et al, 2021). By definition, ICT occurs within the family context and is perpetrated by someone who is considered a child's family member or caretaker.

In a recent development, ICT is different from most physical abuse, which is episodic and often impulsive. Most physical abuse results from parents losing control and/or accidentally hurting a child more than intended. Part of the harm of ICT is its insidious and all-encompassing nature; the child has few avenues for healthy development.

While ICT is thought to be relatively rare, it's still common enough that anyone who works with children or families over a decade is apt to encounter a child who has been or is being tortured. Often, the professional will mistake the ICT for simple abuse or neglect, and will fail to offer the child meaningful assistance.

We have each seen more than a few cases of ICT over the course of our professional lives (Miller about 50, Fontes about 15). Many professionals have never heard of ICT. But even when they have, they might mistakenly discard the ICT framework if the case before them doesn’t seem to fit their idea of what ICT looks like. This can have fatal consequences.

Industry observers note that our goal here is to expand professionals’ internal schema of how ICT appears by discussing diverse presentations that we’ve encountered. This is a stand-in until research devises undoubtedly different, more robust, evidence-based typologies. We link descriptions to real cases in the popular media, so readers can learn more.

Parents who torture their children don’t necessarily lead marginal lives. They may be wealthy professionals and appear to be caring and competent in their work lives (Miller et al., 2021). Ruby Franke, a parenting influencer, appears to have tortured her children and eventually pleaded guilty to aggravated child abuse. Larry and Carri Williams were popular at their church before their convictions involving assault on one child and the death by torture of another.

While most family violence is committed by men, some ICT involves a female caregiver as the primary perpetrator. Adoptive mother Maribel Loera recently pleaded guilty to second-degree murder, concealment of a body, and multiple counts of severe child abuse, thus avoiding the death penalty. According to media reports, two of her surviving children testified to years of severe violence, including burns, beatings, and a knife attack that left permanent scars. Professionals should be aware that ICT can be driven by female perpetrators.

It has been revealed that some child torturers’ lives follow a pattern of abuse and withdrawal from drugs; they could be especially dangerous at any part of this cycle. They may act in extremely harmful ways when “out of their wits” from alcohol, methamphetamines, fentanyl, or other substances. However, while the substances may make episodic violence more intense or more frequent, the substances are not the cause. By definition, ICT is purposeful and deliberate.

Recent findings suggest that while there is plentiful research on the higher prevalence of child abuse and neglect among caregivers who abuse substances, we were unable to find research on child torture specifically. But we’ve both seen drug-addled caretakers who seem to have lost any sense of care or morality and torture a child or children over time, sometimes fatally.

The first study to analyze a large body of ICT cases statistically (Rycus et al. 2026) found that non-biological parents are more likely to be perpetrators of ICT than biological parents. This includes stepparents, biological parents’ romantic partners, adoptive parents, foster parents, and relatives caring for children. The case of Larry and Carri Williams (mentioned above) stands out here, where parents of seven biological children adopted two children from Ethiopia, and the mother tortured the older child, Hana, until she died from malnutrition and hypothermia. While the parents used abusive punishments with their biological children, they apparently tortured only their adopted children.

According to recent reports, sometimes one partner (usually but not always the man in heterosexual couples) coercively controls and tortures not just one or more children, but also his adult partner. In fact, the abuser’s torture of the children may be aimed at dominating his adult partner.

The abuser’s coercive control over his partner incapacitates her ability to protect the children effectively. She may try to deflect the abuser’s rage towards herself. She may sneak the children food when they are locked in the closet. Adult victims may fail to contact authorities due to a combination of fear that their children will be removed and fear that the abuser will kill them and the children before police arrive.

According to recent reports, vanity Fair reported that when the police came to arrest attorney Joel Steinberg and his girlfriend, Editor Hedda Nussbaum, for the death of their adoptive child, Lisa Steinberg, Nussbaum looked like a boxer who had sustained beatings. Nussbaum had a fractured nose and jaw, nine broken ribs, and gangrenous legs.

Sources indicate that in some ICT cases, the parent(s) abuse all the children (e.g., the Turpins, Nixmary Brown, the family of Elisa Izquierdo). In others, the parents seem to differentiate among the children, targeting those children who are not biologically related (as in Hana Williams), who are the oldest, or who are disabled.

Sources indicate that many caretakers hide their tortured children from public view by homeschooling or “no- schooling” them. The under-regulation of homeschooling allows caretakers to torture children with no oversight from teachers or school officials who might otherwise make child abuse reports (Bartholet, 2020). In a typical case, the Hart parents removed their six adopted children from public school after reports of suspected child abuse. In several of the cases mentioned here, the caregivers withdrew the children from school, including the Turpin, Franke, and Williams cases.

At first glance, it might seem that anyone who tortures a child is “crazy.” However, research is lacking on the possible diagnoses of caretakers who torture their children. In our experience, ICT is often perpetrated by people who show no outward signs of mental illness. People in an acute psychotic episode might kill their children, perhaps thinking that this will “save” them or because they are suffering from persecutory delusions or postpartum psychosis. However, this filicide would fail to meet the criteria of ICT as a deliberate and prolonged series of acts.

In a recent development, sometimes organized groups participate in children’s torture. These can include cults, along with sex and labor trafficking networks. These networks often include adult family members who inflict or permit the abuse, thus qualifying as ICT. One example is Children of God (now renamed Family International), where children were routinely beaten, whipped, sexually abused, and denied education. Sex trafficking of minors involves physical and psychological torture as well as neglect, thus qualifying as ICT when family members are involved.

Caregivers who torture their children can be of high or low social status; related by blood or not; substance abusing or sober; of any gender; and loving or cruel to other children in the home. They are apt to keep the tortured child hidden from public view, through home or no-schooling, or networks organized around cults or crime. Learn about ICT so you can tune in to signs that children you suspect are abused may be suffering far worse: torture.

In a recent development, larian Studios has delivered what was arguably the biggest reveal of The Game Awards 2025 showcase. The Hellstone, the mysterious monolith in the desert that’s been generating a lot of speculation in the lead-up to the show was indeed teasing the studio’s next game.

The Belgian developer is returning to the series it created with Divinity, a non-numbered sequel that’s designed for new and veteran players alike. The announcement was entirely cinematic, setting the tone for what looks to be the next big thing in the space.

According to recent reports, larian calls Divinity its most ambitious title ever, with the studio striving for a level of depth and breadth we’ve not seen before. This is the next project from the Baldur’s Gate 3 team, after all, so there’s understandably immense anticipation for it.

Divinity is a standalone RPG, and does not require you to have played Divinity: Original Sin, or Divinity: Original Sin 2. If you did, however, you’re going to find the journey extra special because of the continuity it offers.

“We’re ready to bring everything we’ve done previously into one place,” said founder and game director, Swen Vincke.

In a recent development, “This marks the beginning of something with more breadth, depth, and intimacy than anything we’ve created before. We’ve been building toward this moment ever since we took our fate into our own hands. This is the Divinity we’ve always wanted to make and you're going to have loads of fun with it.”.

Beyond that, there’s precious little that’s been revealed for Divinity so far. We don’t know what platforms it’s going to be coming to, nor do we even have a release target. We do know it’s an RPG, so you can very much expect something similar to earlier games in the series, and, of course, Baldur’s Gate 3.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that the result, called Project B-Zero, looks like a ’55 Chevy from the curb and like a Model 3 as soon as you open the door.
  • In the shop’s latest video, “The First Ever Electric Bel Air,” founder and CEO Ryan Friedlinghaus explains that a longtime client, Troy Swope, wants to convert an entire car collection to electric and picked the Bel Air to go first.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that west Coast Customs has finished its first electric Chevy Bel Air, and there’s not much Chevy left under the paint. The Burbank shop cut the body off a Tesla Model 3, kept the entire rolling platform, and set a 1955 Bel Air shell on top of it.

Industry observers note that the result, called Project B-Zero, looks like a ’55 Chevy from the curb and like a Model 3 as soon as you open the door. And it charges at Tesla Superchargers.

In the shop’s latest video, “The First Ever Electric Bel Air,” founder and CEO Ryan Friedlinghaus explains that a longtime client, Troy Swope, wants to convert an entire car collection to electric and picked the Bel Air to go first. WCC had previously built the same client a Chevelle with a massive gas engine.

Friedlinghaus, who drives a Tesla himself, decided against pulling the Model 3’s motors and battery out and fitting them into the old Chevy. Instead, the Tesla stays whole and the Chevy becomes the body kit.

That’s a formula WCC has used for years with gas cars. The shop calls it “old school meets fresh school”: an old GTO body on a new GTO, an old Camaro on a new Camaro, an old Mustang on a new Mustang. B-Zero is the first time it did it with a Tesla underneath.

“It sounds easy, but that process was tedious,” Friedlinghaus stated.

Before any Chevy sheet metal went on, the crew took the bare Model 3 skateboard for a spin on the streets around the shop, with no doors, no lights and no seatbelts. Friedlinghaus joked about how many safety violations they were racking up. But it drove fine.

The real headache was the wheelbase. A 1955 Chevy rides on a 115-inch wheelbase, while the Model 3 sits at 113.2 inches. On its gas builds, WCC can cut, shorten or lengthen the newer car’s frame to match the old body. You can’t do that with a Tesla, since the floor is the battery pack.

So the shop changed the body instead, stretching the Bel Air’s rear wheel wells so the wheels sit where they look like they belong.

The client wanted the exterior to read as a mostly stock Bel Air. The original car was red, so WCC kept it red, with a satin finish and gloss black accents.

Recent findings suggest that inside, it’s a Model 3. The shop kept the Tesla’s interior, including the steering wheel and center touchscreen, and modified it to fit the Chevy body. The seats got black suede with white stitching in an octagon pattern that Friedlinghaus remarked was borrowed from the Lamborghini Urus, plus red accents and a “B-Zero” script on the dash.

Friedlinghaus said the goal was for people to see “a really nice Bel Air” from the outside, then open the door and find a Tesla. He also expects some double takes when it pulls into a Supercharger station.

He admits the reaction has been split. Plenty of people are mad that the shop electrified a Bel Air, and plenty of others think it came out great. The client is clearly in the second camp, describing the car as easy to drive and saying every trip in it feels like an event.

Here’s the full build video from West Coast Customs:.

This is sick. I know Tesla doesn’t care about personal car ownership anymore, but they should really sell their platform so shops can do these conversions without using salvage vehicles.

Well I was really interested in this build until I read how they kept it entirely Tesla inside. Not at all what I was thinking or what I'd call a true old car conversion to EV. Instead, they simply transformed the outside of a Tesla into an old looking car. To me, even the outside looks too far removed from the original Bel Air and more like a street rod. If that's what the owner wants and paid for, great.

But for me, I would never do a conversion like that. I really want to convert an older 70's or 80's or early 90's Cadillac into an EV. But for me, I will insist that the outside and inside look 100% like the original car with just an EV powertrain.

Don’t get me wrong, if you can recycle a salvage, that’s good, but it can’t always be done.

Compare it to the 1966 Mustang that a Sacramento Tesla parts shop converted earlier this year. That project took about $40,000 and two years, with the team grafting sections of a Model 3 floor into the Mustang. It’s an amazing build, but it’s a lot of custom engineering. WCC’s approach skips most of that. You keep Tesla’s crash structure, battery thermal management, software, over-the-air updates and Supercharger access, because you never took the car apart in the first place. It’s closer to what S-Klub did with its Model 3-based Mercedes 300SL than a traditional drivetrain swap.

Sources indicate that the purists will hate it. That’s fine. This Bel Air will get driven more in a year than most restored ones get driven in a decade.

Every Brand Still Selling Sports Cars | Our Top-Rated Car Brands | Future Cars Worth Waiting For.

Sources indicate that nothing turns a head quite like a Ferrari, and we think the mid-engined 296 is the stunner of the current lineup. It looks fantastic as both a coupe and as a convertible. The active rear spoiler manages to maintain the sports car’s sleek profile whether it’s engaged or not, and the low nose with a thin, sweeping grille is classic Ferrari. The 296 drives as good as it looks, too, thanks to its hybrid powertrain that uses a twin-turbo V-6 engine.

The Miata has been an enthusiast staple since it entered the market wide-eyed and grinning in 1990. Since then, it’s grown up a bit, replacing pop-up headlights with angular, cat-like eyes and turning the grin into a bit more of a snarl. It’s a head-turner in any generation, but the newest ND is the sportiest model yet, and it’s best enjoyed with the top down. We also love the look of the Retractable Fastback (RF) body style pictured here. For an incredibly fun and affordable sports car, the Miata is truly always the answer.

More About the Mazda MX-5 Miata.

While the Genesis brand isn’t quite as well-established as Mercedes or BMW, its flagship G90 looks every bit the part of a luxury sedan. Thin, sweeping taillights punctuate the nicely shaped rear end, while the classic diamond-shaped grille integrates beautifully with the slim, low-profile headlights. The G90 looks, sounds, and feels silky, and its sub-$100,000 starting price tag is surprising given how special it is.

It has been revealed that like the G90, the GV70’s sophisticated design language helps it punch above its weight against the Porsches and Mercedes-Benzes in its segment. The GV70’s sporty body lines and interior details, including a knurled glass shift knob, make it feel like a true luxury vehicle. Genesis added a Prestige Graphite trim to the lineup for 2027, which makes the GV70 look even sportier with carbon-fiber pieces, darkened trim, and red brake calipers.

When Maserati brought back the GranTurismo nameplate in 2024, the sports car got a subtle redesign that brought out all of the best qualities found in the previous generation. Since then, it’s only gotten better thanks to a styling refresh for 2027. With a cheerfully aggressive front end and a sloped, sleek rear that tapers nicely, the GranTurismo coupe exudes high-performance fun in a stylish two-door package.

More About the Maserati GranTurismo.

Recent findings suggest that the Lotus Emira looks great from any angle, and its gorgeously proportioned styling rivals much more expensive exotics. The Emira is a true stripped-back sports car, with just the necessities inside the cabin and a heavy focus on performance and agility. It’s unmistakably a mid-engined car, as the rear fenders flare out to make room for the hefty air intakes behind the doors, and the sleek roofline melts seamlessly into an angular rear end for a spunky-yet-elegant silhouette.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arc Raiders is kicking off its last major event of the year. The Cold Snap update arrives moments from now, and it’s perhaps the game’s biggest since its momentous launch in late October. We’ve known about the existence of Cold Snap for a while, of course, but we finally have a solid idea about what to expect.

Cold Snap is made up of different components - including new content - that all players have access to.

As the name suggests, of course, Cold Snap introduces the new snowfall Map Condition. As part of this, maps will be covered in snow, thanks to snowstorms sweeping across them. For one, snowfall makes it harder to see enemies, but it also turns all lakes solid.

Recent findings suggest that there’s a newly introduced mechanic associated with this, and it’s actually similar to Battlefield 6’s Winter Offensive patch. Staying outdoors for too long will cause you to catch frostbite, which slowly drains HP. Embark indicates you’re going to need to bring more healing items with you on raids, and it doesn’t look like there are firepits that could keep you warm - though staying indoors for a while will help.

According to recent reports, cold Snap arrives alongside limited-time events that will be available until Tuesday, January 13. The snowfall visual update and upcoming frostbite mechanics are available on Dam Battlegrounds, Buried City, Spaceport, and The Blue Gate.

Sources indicate that one of the upcoming events is Flickering Flames, which comes with its own progression track of 25 levels. Industry observers note that volkswagen’s EV push in America has skewed practical, for the most part. The ID.4 was a generic crossover, so close to an electric take on the Tiguan that VW is actually rebranding it as the ID. Tiguan. And the ID. Buzz, whimsical styling aside, is an electric van—a very expensive electric van. But VW has not abandoned its small, fun hatchback roots in Europe, and the German brand is continuing the celebration of the 50th anniversary of its GTI sub-brand with an EV: the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept, which it will debut at the Essen Motorshow later this month.

The ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept is an all-electric, track-ready, front-wheel drive hot hatch. VW shoehorned an electric drive system intended for larger RWD vehicles into the sub-compact ID. Polo GTI; that gives the concept outputs of 362 horsepower (up to 389 hp in short bursts) and 406 pound-feet of torque, a massive increase from the 223 hp and 214 lb-ft in the standard model.

The ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept can hit a top speed of 149 mph, and it can accelerate from 0-60 mph in 4.7 seconds—quicker than a Golf GTI but not quite as quick as a gas-powered Golf R—with the launch control engaged.

This VW’s body is heavily modified from the standard model, as well. It features a two-door layout instead of four, flared fenders, and an enormous front splitter, diffuser, and rear wing. VW also stripped out the interior for track work by deleting the rear seat and cargo area. The two front seats are Recaro racing bucket seats with five-point harnesses, and the interior also has an integrated Tornado Red roll bar.

It has been revealed that sadly, this is just a concept for now. Volkswagen has not committed to building an ID. Polo GTI Clubsport, and even if the brand did, it would be unlikely to be offered in the American market. VW did reveal a very cool ID. GTI concept back in 2023, which it has claimed will be more fun than the combustion-powered GTIs. And Volkswagen, pointedly, has not ruled out bringing that car to America—though getting the pricing and timing right in the U.S., with an unstable tariff situation and variable EV incentive climate, may prove tricky.

#166898. How Italians Cured My Loneliness

How Italians Cured My Loneliness

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (852 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Updated November 23, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.
  • A couple of years ago, I’d made the painful decision to leave my marriage, and my beloved dog of 13 years had died.
  • The life I had always imagined for myself—a long-term stable marriage and a family nested in community—had never materialized.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Updated November 23, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.

A couple of years ago, I’d made the painful decision to leave my marriage, and my beloved dog of 13 years had died. Suddenly, I found myself deeply alone.

The life I had always imagined for myself—a long-term stable marriage and a family nested in community—had never materialized.

One day, though, I realized that there was something that I had dreamed of when I was younger, that suddenly might be possible.

Industry observers note that I went. And I went again. I discovered a lesser-known town in my favorite area, and an affordable apartment that I could use periodically in the off-season. I committed to going, using airline points, when I had lulls between stretches of speaking engagements.

Because of my youthful obsession with all things Italian, I had studied the language. I’d also had a long-distance Italian boyfriend for a few months in my early 30s.

I brushed up via a language app, and this was the key that opened all doors.

In Canada, I was a solitary woman who had to book appointments to see her busy friends, all of whom had families.

In Italy, I found myself swept up into a large, generous family and their circle of friends, and rarely had enough time to sit and read a book.

The way I learned to live in Italy transformed the way I live at home.

I always thought my phone aversion was due to being an introvert. Even if the name on my screen was a friend, I’d send it to voicemail and text them a little bit later.

In Italy, I discovered the delight of being interrupted.

Recent findings suggest that at least once a day, my friend Vincenza knocked at my door unannounced, calling out my name. My old Canadian self might have pretended not to be home, but I began to associate these unexpected visits with delight. Vincenza usually had a plate of hot pasta or pastries in her arms, or her sister Angela would call to invite me for lunch.

Sources indicate that the effect stuck. Today, when a friend or family member calls me, I find myself answering. Sometimes I even call them.

Sources indicate that part of why I wouldn’t answer the phone when it rang was because it wasn’t part of "the initiative." I ran a tight ship. Or perhaps not actually that tight, because I was usually already behind on the day’s to-do list. There wasn’t room for an unplanned 15-minute chat with a friend.

In Italy, Angela randomly calls to let me know that they’ll gather in the piazza in 10 minutes “because the sun is so beautiful today.”.

An impromptu lunch invitation may stretch into a couple of hours around a table with friends.

When I run into Vincenza’s daughter, Nausica, while out running errands, she often invites me for a spontaneous coffee or aperitivo, or to go to a store around the corner and help her pick out a dress for an event.

In my past life, I believed that because I was doing something (anything) else, the natural answer was, "Sorry, not now.".

I’ve learned that unless I absolutely must be doing something else, the best answer is “Sure, why not?”.

If you’ve seen the meme of the hyper-independent woman carrying a clothes washer up the subway steps by herself, that’s me.

In a recent development, I don’t like needing or asking for help. I am, however, a professional helper. Literally. I’m a medical doctor, an executive coach, and a professional speaker/educator. Perhaps most importantly, I’m also the first-born daughter of four.

I will help you with things you didn’t even know you needed help with.

In a recent development, then there are my Italian friends. They don’t need my help. They don’t seem to even want my help.

It has been revealed that they stealthily pay for my aperitivo or pizza, sneaking the waiter money while pretending to use the washroom. I once tried to pay for parking, and my friend wrestled me out of the way so intensely that I hesitate to ever attempt it again.

Industry observers note that but what about medical help? Surely, there might be potential for heroics. Nope, they already have a doctor in the family.

Industry observers note that the thing is, they seem to just enjoy having me around—without me doing anything other than showing up and eating the food they place in front of me, with great enthusiasm. This seems to be all one needs to do to earn permanently adopted status.

Recent findings suggest that I think that was the ultimate blow that broke the chains of my very North American loneliness. In a “What can you do for me?” world, it’s remarkable to discover a collective of people, all of whom seem to live by the same rules: “You’ll always have a place at my table—just don’t argue when I serve you more pasta.”.

Tesla toughens FSD driver monitoring in Europe while loosening it in the US

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1131 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla is rolling out stricter driver monitoring for its “Full Self-Driving” system in Europe, with earlier warnings, a full strike for drivers who look away during a manoeuvre, and a hands-on-wheel requirement above 130 km/h (81 mph).
  • According to recent reports, in the US, Tesla has spent the last year going the other way.
  • Sources indicate that on November 16, the Dutch vehicle authority RDW unveiled that it signed off on a fresh revision to Tesla Assisted Driving, the name Tesla now uses for FSD (Supervised) in Europe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla is rolling out stricter driver monitoring for its “Full Self-Driving” system in Europe, with earlier warnings, a full strike for drivers who look away during a manoeuvre, and a hands-on-wheel requirement above 130 km/h (81 mph).

According to recent reports, in the US, Tesla has spent the last year going the other way. Its CEO told owners they can text and drive on FSD, and recent US builds were tuned to nag drivers less.

Sources indicate that on November 16, the Dutch vehicle authority RDW unveiled that it signed off on a fresh revision to Tesla Assisted Driving, the name Tesla now uses for FSD (Supervised) in Europe. It covers HW4 vehicles and goes out over the air.

In a recent development, according to the RDW, drivers now get attention warnings earlier. If a driver isn’t paying attention while the system performs a manoeuvre, they get a “full strike.” The regulator indicates the patch also adds measures to prevent misuse of the system, but it didn’t spell out what they are.

There’s a speed component too. Above 130 km/h (where legal), the driver has to keep their hands on the wheel. And setting a maximum speed above what the system displays now requires the driver to confirm it by scrolling the wheel up, with the speed limit sign pulsing red when the car goes over.

It has been revealed that the RDW notes it tested the enhancement on its own track and on public roads and found no adverse or unintended effects. Ten other countries have adopted the Dutch approval so far, with Finland now on the list, while EU-wide approval is still waiting on a vote at the TCMV, the committee of member states.

According to recent reports, this comes two weeks after Tesla cut the system’s speed margin from 50% to 10% over the limit in Europe and dropped the “Full Self-Driving” name there. Germany had made both a condition of supporting EU approval.

Now look at how Tesla handles the same software at home.

At Tesla’s shareholder meeting last November, Musk complained that the car was “a little strict about keeping your eyes on the road” and said Tesla would “allow you to text and drive essentially” within a month or two. A month later, an owner asked whether FSD v14.2.1 allowed texting. Musk’s answer: “Depending on context of surrounding traffic, yes.”.

Sources indicate that texting while driving is illegal in 49 states. FSD is still a Level 2 system, and Tesla’s own fine print says the driver is responsible at all times.

In May, Musk confirmed that FSD v14.3.3 was built to nag drivers less. Tesla did add better eye-gaze tracking and eyewear handling in a June build, to be fair. But the pitch to owners hasn’t changed: fewer nags is sold as a feature.

In a recent development, and US drivers have been allowed to go hands-free on FSD at any speed since Tesla moved to cabin-camera monitoring in 2024. There’s no 130 km/h rule here.

NHTSA noticed. In its engineering analysis of FSD crashes in low-visibility conditions, the agency asked Tesla to justify a list of its marketing claims, and it specifically cited Musk’s texting post. In September, Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi asked NHTSA to look into Tesla’s driver monitoring after dozens of videos appeared to show drivers asleep on Autopilot and FSD.

Sources indicate that the results are on the road. Last month, a driver told the CHP he was asleep on FSD when his Tesla drove through a freeway closure and hit a patrol car, seriously injuring two officers. Owners are also filming themselves defeating Tesla’s driver monitoring and posting it for clout.

Both markets get the same cabin camera and the same HW4 computer.

In a recent development, but in Europe, a type-approval authority tests every revision before it ships and can refuse it. In the US, nobody pre-approves driver-assist software. Tesla self-certifies, and NHTSA only steps in after complaints and crashes pile up, which is how you end up with a CEO publicly telling owners to text while the regulator is still writing letters about it.

Industry observers note that this upgrade proves Tesla can build stricter driver monitoring whenever a regulator demands it. The code exists. It’s running on HW4 cars in 11 European countries right now.

That's because Musk is buddies with the current federal government that would regulate his not-full-self-driving system. Whereas Europe doesn't kowtow to his whims. We'll see what happens in 2029 with a new administration.

That makes the US approach hard to defend. Tesla’s argument for relaxing supervision is that FSD is now good enough. But if that were true, it would be showing the RDW data proving looser monitoring is safe, not adding earlier warnings and harsher strikes to get approved. It’s doing the opposite in Europe because it has to, and the opposite of that in the US because it can.

In a recent development, we’ve been saying it for a while: FSD gets more dangerous as it gets better, because people trust it more and watch the road less. The answer is monitoring that tightens as the system improves. Europe is forcing exactly that. In the US, Tesla is loosening it, encouraging illegal phone use from the top, and leaving drivers with 100% of the liability when it goes wrong.

In a recent development, so here’s the question for Tesla. If European owners are getting earlier warnings and instant strikes, why not American owners on the exact same software? Or is NHTSA going to have to force it?

#166894. Kia went from this one quirky EV 40 years ago to an entire electric lineup

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (625 w)

EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Kia went from this one quirky EV 40 years ago to an entire electric lineup

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (625 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Kia Besta EV hit the roads in 1986 as the brand’s first fully electric vehicle.
  • Kia wanted to design a new vehicle for the 1986 Asian Games, which were held in Seoul, South Korea, one that did not emit any toxic fumes in front of runners.
  • The Besta van was initially developed 40 years ago by Kia’s Central Research Institute as the successor to the popular Bongo van, which is still sold in Korea and other markets today.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Kia Besta EV hit the roads in 1986 as the brand’s first fully electric vehicle. 40 years later, Kia continues to “lead the pack” with a full lineup of EVs ranging from entry-level cars and SUVs to three-row models, and just about everything in between.

Kia wanted to design a new vehicle for the 1986 Asian Games, which were held in Seoul, South Korea, one that did not emit any toxic fumes in front of runners.

So, it created the Besta EV. The Besta van was initially developed 40 years ago by Kia’s Central Research Institute as the successor to the popular Bongo van, which is still sold in Korea and other markets today.

Unlike the Bongo, it was developed using Kia’s in-house tech rather than sourced from another automaker and rebadged as its own.

Kia swapped the 2.0L four-cylinder diesel engine for a 35 kWh battery and electric motor, which provided a range of more than 26 miles (42 km) on a single charge.

While the Besta EV was never actually sold to the public, it laid the groundwork and offered an early glimpse at Kia’s shift to electrification.

In a recent development, the first mass-produced Korean EV certified for commercial sale was the Kia Pride EV in 1993. In 2011, the Ray EV became Kia’s first series-production electric car.

Kia expanded its electrification ambitions to Europe and the UK in 2014 with the first-generation Soul EV, the beloved boxy, funky crossover that was discontinued after the 2025 model year.

The Korean automaker has come a long way since the Besta EV, with a full lineup of electric vehicles ranging from compact cars to mid-size and three-row SUVs, vans, and just about everything in between.

Kia now offers an electric option for nearly everyone with seven-passenger EVs on sale in the UK and Europe, including the EV2, EV3, EV4, EV5, EV6, EV9, and PV5 Passenger van.

With its first software-defined vehicle (SDV) and a new B-segment electric hatchback set to launch by the end of 2027, Kia has no prepares to slow down. On top of this, Kia will expand its PBV lineup with the PV7 next year, a larger sibling to the PV5.

Four decades after the Besta EV arrived, Kia said it continues to “lead the pack today” with one of the most diverse all-electric EV lineups of any brand.

Through October, Kia has sold over 135,000 EVs in the UK, with fully electric vehicles now accounting for over 37% of total sales.

Thanks to its fresh EV lineup, Kia became “Europe’s fastest-growing top 10 passenger-car brand.” According to the European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association, Kia registered 377,078 vehicles between January and August 2026, up 9% compared to the same period last year.

Sjoerd Knipping, Chief Operating Officer of Kia Europe, remarked the growth is thanks to having “one of the broadest and most advanced electrified line-ups in Europe.”.

It has been revealed that in the US, Kia introduced the compact EV3 (check out our review of it) this year, starting at just $29,890. It joins the EV6, EV9, and Niro EV in Kia’s US electric vehicle lineup.

Arc Raiders' latest patch adds two of the most requested features, but kills Cred hoarding

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that embark has just rolled out patch 1.7.0 for Arc Raiders players everywhere.
  • Dig deeper into the patch notes, however, and you’ll find even more to get excited about, including features players have been asking for since the game’s first public test.
  • It has been revealed that to start with, today’s enhancement finally adds an option toggle aiming down sights.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that embark has just rolled out patch 1.7.0 for Arc Raiders players everywhere. This is a significant patch for the extraction shooter for a number of reasons, not least of which because it kicks off a series of events under the Cold Snap banner, which introduces a upcoming conditions to the game’s maps.

Dig deeper into the patch notes, however, and you’ll find even more to get excited about, including features players have been asking for since the game’s first public test.

It has been revealed that to start with, today’s enhancement finally adds an option toggle aiming down sights. This is especially relevant for PC players, most of whom play shooters with an ADS toggle, rather than hold. Another often requested feature has been the ability to reset the game’s skill tree.

Industry observers note that this is now available for the cost of 2,000 Coins per skill point. It goes without saying that you’re going to need a whole lot of money to reset the entire thing, but it’s a useful option to have when you want to alter your path.

The next change is one that’s going to ruffle a lot of feathers. Arc Raiders now has a soft Cred cap of 800. This is now clearly shown on your Wallet screen, and the developer noted the cap is necessary to prevent players from using their accumulated Cred to unlock upcoming Raider Decks immediately after release.

Sources indicate that the good news is that this won’t affect the Cred you may already have, but going forward, 800 is the most you can hold at any point. You’ll also notice that Shani has more stuff for you to buy with Cred, in case you want another way to spend what you have.

Sources indicate that patch 1.7.0 also brings a few other additions - and makes some changes - that are worth highlighting. You can now customise your Raider Tool, which likely means we’re going to see Raider Tool cosmetics going forward.

Speaking of items, the Aphelion weapon blueprint has been moved to Stella Montis, so you won’t be able to get it from taking down the Matriarch. The Bettina, and Rattler have both seen some balance changes.

Industry observers note that the Bettina’s durability will now degrade a lot slower per shot, making it take 26 magazines to fully deplete durability. The base magazine size has been increased to 22, and the reload time has been cut to 4.5 seconds. Embark states this should make the weapon more viable in PvP, while also allowing it to stand on its own without the need for players bring a secondary weapon.

It has been revealed that as for the Rattler, the only change it gets is an increase to its magazine size from 10 to 12. The idea is to make it about as effective as a Stitcher or Kettle at close ranges when it comes to PvP encounters.

According to recent reports, and, of course, it wouldn’t be a massive Arc Raiders patch without some tweaks to the game’s Arc enemies. This time, the Shredder gets all the love. The menacing unit now moves faster, turns more sharply and doesn’t get knocked back as much when shot.

The Shredder’s head now has more health, too, meaning you won’t be able to shoot it off early and confuse it. In general, the Arc unit should be smarter, especially when navigating narrow spaces. Finally, the Shredder now activates faster upon detecting (and being attacked by) players.

Beyond that, the main menu has seen a few changes to highlight ongoing events, make certain announcements quieter, make it easier to track Raider Quests and more. There’s a lot more in this update, too, such as changes to footstep loudness, several tweaks to loot and the value of certain items, and more besides. You’ll find the full change log on the official website.

#166889. Why Kissing Matters More Than You Think During Sex

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (959 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

Why Kissing Matters More Than You Think During Sex

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (959 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 23, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.
  • Recent findings suggest that in today’s sexual landscape, we are getting a lot of information about how to supercharge our sex lives.
  • It has been revealed that researcher Lisa Wade (2017) found that in hook-up culture, people tend to follow the “no kissing during sex” rule to preserve boundaries, ostensibly keeping sex casual and emotionally safe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 23, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.

Recent findings suggest that in today’s sexual landscape, we are getting a lot of information about how to supercharge our sex lives. There are Instagram ads for vibrators and other accessories, shelves of toys at our local drugstore, and no end of supplements marketed to anyone whose libido might be waning. But the data tells us that actually our strongest—but most undervalued—predictor of satisfying sex is just good old-fashioned kissing. And this is as true for people hooking up with new partners as it is for those in long-term relationships.

So why has kissing fallen out of fashion?

It has been revealed that researcher Lisa Wade (2017) found that in hook-up culture, people tend to follow the “no kissing during sex” rule to preserve boundaries, ostensibly keeping sex casual and emotionally safe. But that strategy for avoiding feeling too close to a casual partner can have an unintended consequence. Eschewing kissing can, as my own students report, leave them feeling empty afterward. For long-term partners, kissing can be bypassed out of time constraints and a misguided attempt at sexual efficiency. When you are trying to squeeze sex in around busy jobs or parenting, it can be tempting to “jump to the main event.” Meanwhile, both groups can be influenced by porn that emphasizes novel activities like choking over “vanilla” activities like kissing. But the research highlights that forgoing kissing to keep sex casual or efficient skips the activity that most reliably predicts it being good, and it’s women who pay the price.

When researchers Busby et al. (2021) set out to quantify the impact of kissing on relationship and sexual satisfaction in long-term relationships, they found that both specific kissing (during the most recent sexual experience) and global kissing (during the last year) were positively associated with their subjects’ perspective on the quality of their sex lives and their overall relationship satisfaction. For women, kissing during sex was positively associated with their ability to orgasm, sexual frequency, and indirectly with sexual satisfaction. Because they were more likely to orgasm, this positive reinforcement made them want to have sex more often, creating a virtuous feedback loop. These findings suggest that kissing shouldn’t be thought of as superfluous, but rather reclassified as foundational to relationship maintenance and a couple’s sexual repertoire.

According to recent reports, while both sexes associate more kissing with a stronger relationship, the orgasm benefits definitely skew toward women. Kissing signals emotional closeness, slows the pace of the encounter, and extends foreplay, all of which raise arousal and make orgasm more likely for women.

This is why Wade’s research into hooking up with an understanding that kissing is off the table sets women at a disadvantage. When researcher Frederick and his team (2017) asked a cross-sample of people if their last sexual encounter led to orgasm, unsurprisingly, 65 percent of heterosexual women answered affirmatively compared to 95 percent of heterosexual men. This is called the orgasm gap. Kissing can help close that gap even for upcoming partners.

It has been revealed that in addition to incorporating specific kissing back into sex, pay attention to global kissing. The above studies are correlational, but this study isn’t: Kory Floyd and colleagues (2009) assigned married and cohabiting couples to kiss more for six weeks. Compared with controls, the kissing group had lower stress, lower cholesterol, and higher relationship satisfaction. In a classic “fake it till you make it” framework, starting with increasing kissing can lead to a stronger relationship, rather than waiting for events to unfold the other way around.

New research from Christopher Watkins and Milena Rota (2026) found that fantasy and sexual imagination inform the perception of a good kiss rather than technique. And even more important than technique is duration. The Gottmans claim that as long as a kiss lasts at least six seconds, the brain releases oxytocin, which is the bonding hormone that enables all of the above (Brittle, 2014).

So, in our overscheduled, overstimulating world, think about coming back to basics. If your sex life has gone flat, kissing is the easiest place to start because it’s free, you can’t run out, its batteries won’t go dead, and best of all, it brings both people into the moment. That's what great sex is all about.

#166888. Potatoes grown in moon dirt are as nutritious as Earth potatoes

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (561 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Popsci ↗ Open Full Page

Potatoes grown in moon dirt are as nutritious as Earth potatoes

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (561 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Astronauts living in the first permanent lunar base may see a sizable number of spuds on their dinner plates.
  • “We found that potatoes can complete their entire life cycle in simulated lunar soil when supplemented with organic matter,” Aymeric Goyer, an OSU botanist and study co-author, said in a statement.
  • Even in a controlled habitat, life on the moon will be physically demanding for astronauts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Astronauts living in the first permanent lunar base may see a sizable number of spuds on their dinner plates. In a study published today in the journal npj Microgravity, botanists at Oregon State University (OSU) proved it’s possible to grow healthy, edible potatoes in simulated moon soil with the help of everyday worms. Importantly, the team also identified the proper proportions of lunar regolith and compost needed to produce potato yields similar to those grown on Earth.

“We found that potatoes can complete their entire life cycle in simulated lunar soil when supplemented with organic matter,” Aymeric Goyer, an OSU botanist and study co-author, said in a statement. “That’s an important step toward developing reliable food production systems that could support long-term human exploration of the Moon.”.

Even in a controlled habitat, life on the moon will be physically demanding for astronauts. They’ll require carefully maintained, nutritious diets to keep them healthy, but it’s not as simple as sending them off packed with calorically dense prepackaged meals. Cargo room on spacecraft is limited and costly, and the desolate lunar surface isn’t exactly hospitable to agriculture. In addition to constant bombardment by cosmic and solar radiation, temperatures can swing anywhere between 250 degrees and -410 degrees Fahrenheit.

Indoor horticulture will also be challenging. Lunar regolith is an annoyingly powdery substance composed of sharp-edged, miniscule particles created over billions of years of asteroid impacts, but little else. With essentially no organic material at all, the dust alone isn’t capable of supporting plant life.

While it is easy enough to combine that lunar regolith with agricultural additives, researchers weren’t sure if these could overcome moon soil’s heavy metals and irradiation. To test it, Goyer and his colleagues first obtained simulated lunar regolith made to resemble the samples collected during the Apollo missions. Regolith composition varies by region on the moon, so they selected five different types based on darker lunar mare dust and the lighter lunar highland soil. They then mixed the mock moon dust with vermicompost, the nutrient-rich soil created when worms break down organic materials. Next, they planted potatoes in various ratios of regolith and vermicompost, and monitored their growth. As a control, the team even planted potatoes in soil taken from Hermiston, Oregon, an area famous for some of the world’s highest spud yields.

In a recent development, the team found that composite soil with only 30 percent vermicompost was enough to produce potato crops comparable to those farmed on Earth. Their findings suggest the supplemental organics bind to the regolith’s heavy metals, which shield the plants and minimize any damage to their roots.

“We believe the compost helps balance some of the toxicity we see in lunar regolith,” added OSU botanist and study co-author David Handy.

But bushels of moon potatoes only go so far if they lack any real nutritional value. Even here, the lunar simulations offered promising results, particularly when it came to glycoalkaloids. The naturally forming potato toxins can cause green skin discoloration, but analysis indicated no statistically relevant rise in glycoalkaloids for the lunar crops.

With the potato viability debate settled, Goyer’s team will next compare 10 specific spud varieties grown in simulated lunar regolith to determine the most nutritious and resilient options for NASA astronomers.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that circan’s November 2025 video game sales report has easily been one of the most anticipated.
  • It has been revealed that we’re talking, of course, about Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 the latest releases in their respective multiplayer shooter series.
  • Cricana’s report covers spending on video game software, hardware, and accessories in the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that circan’s November 2025 video game sales report has easily been one of the most anticipated. For one, November is always one of the most lucrative for the games industry, but this year in particular has seen several major hits - including latest entries in two rival series.

It has been revealed that we’re talking, of course, about Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 the latest releases in their respective multiplayer shooter series. The decades-old fight to claim the top spot has long been won by Call of Duty, but the latest Battlefield has achieved what many thought was impossible.

Cricana’s report covers spending on video game software, hardware, and accessories in the U.S. November 2025 saw spending fall by 4% compared to November 2024, bringing in a total of $5.9 billion.

In a recent development, software technically saw growth during the month, but declines in hardware, and accessories were mainly responsible for the drop in overall spending. Black Ops 7 continued Call of Duty’s 18-Year Streak in topping sales in its launch month.

It has been revealed that however, this year’s game did not also top the year-to-date charts, something the series has done consistently, and more than any other top-selling game each year - with rare exceptions. Battlefield 6 is firmly in the lead there, cementing its claim as 2025’s best-selling title. Black Ops 7, fittingly, occupies in the #7 spot there.

Separately from the best-selling game title fight, November has actually been one of the worst for the industry in terms of hardware sales. The report notes that the three major platform holders - Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo have all seen their hardware sales decline.

According to recent reports, spending on hardware during November amounted to only $695 million, a massive 27% decline compared to November 2024. According to the report, that’s the worst dollar amount total for any November since 2005, when it comes to hardware specifically. All three current-gen consoles totaled 1.6 million units sold, which Circana also notes is the lowest for any November since 1995.

This all doesn’t bode especially well for the industry. November has always been a key holiday shopping month, but it’s clear the constantly rising console prices - and already high game prices - have had a significant impact.
